claims.statement: Tsovinar or Nar was the Armenian goddess of water, sea and rain, a fierce goddess who forced rain from the sky with her fury.
claims.statement_id: Tsovinar (Ծովինար) atau Nar adalah dewi air, laut, dan hujan Armenia, dewi garang yang memaksa hujan turun dari langit dengan amarahnya.
claims.quote: or Nar (Նար) was the Armenian goddess of water, sea, and rain. She was a fierce goddess, who forced the rain to fall from the sky with her fury.

claims.statement: Her name means "daughter of the seas", and in Armenian epic tradition she is the mother of Sanasar and Baghdasar.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berarti "putri lautan", dan dalam tradisi epos Armenia ia ibu Sanasar dan Baghdasar.
claims.quote: Her name, Tzovinar, means "daughter of the seas" and she is identified as the mother of Sanasar and Baghdasar in Armenian epic tradition.

claims.statement: Her name has two parts: Armenian tzov, "sea, large body of water", and nar or Nar.
claims.statement_id: Namanya terdiri atas dua bagian: tzov dalam bahasa Armenia, "laut, perairan besar", dan nar atau Nar.
claims.quote: Her name can be decomposed into two parts: Armenian/Old Armenian tzov 'sea, large body of water', and nar or Nar.

claims.statement: Tsovinar, also Tsovyan, is a goddess of ancient Armenian mythology, personification of storm and lightning and goddess of sea, water and rain, riding a fiery horse in the clouds during storms and sending life-giving rain or harmful hail.
claims.statement_id: Tsovinar, juga Tsovyan, adalah dewi dalam mitologi Armenia kuno, perwujudan badai dan petir sekaligus dewi laut, air, dan hujan, yang saat badai menunggang kuda api di awan dan mengirim hujan yang menghidupkan atau hujan es yang merusak.
claims.quote: богиня в древнеармянской мифологии, персонификация грозы, молнии, и одновременно богиня моря, воды, дождя, во время грозы скачущая на огненном коне в облаках; она посылает людям живительный дождь или вредносный град.

claims.statement: In droughts, processions and ritual songs were dedicated to her asking for rain on the fields.
claims.statement_id: Saat kemarau, arak-arakan dan nyanyian ritual dipersembahkan kepadanya dengan permohonan agar hujan turun ke ladang.
claims.quote: Во время засухи ей посвящались шествия и ритуальные песнопения с пожеланиями послать полям дождь.

claims.statement: Tsovinar is King Gagik's daughter, the Caliph of Baghdad's wife and mother of the twins Sanasar and Baghdasar, conceived from two handfuls of sea water she drank.
claims.statement_id: Tsovinar adalah putri Raja Gagik, istri Khalifah Baghdad, dan ibu si kembar Sanasar dan Baghdasar yang ia kandung dari dua genggam air laut yang ia minum.
claims.quote: Цовинар —  дочь царя Гагика, жена Багдадского Халифа, мать первых сасунских героев близнецов Санасара и Багдасара, зачатых ею от выпитых ею двух пригоршней морской воды.

claims.statement: In 1973 composer Grigor Akhinian wrote the opera "Tsovinar".
claims.statement_id: Pada 1973 komposer Grigor Akhinian menulis opera "Tsovinar".
claims.quote: В 1973 году композитор Григор Ахинян написал оперу «Цовинар».

issues.message: Diusulkan dilewati: Bukan makhluk: menurut sumber, zduhać adalah manusia (kadang hewan) yang diyakini punya kemampuan bawaan melindungi desa dari cuaca buruk. Sesuai aturan 3 Oktober 2026 (§12), manusia tidak dimasukkan. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zduha%C4%87).

claims.statement: Zmei (masculine) and zmeya (feminine), meaning "serpent", is a form of dragon in Russian folktales and epic poetry, sometimes a human-like character with dragon traits.
claims.statement_id: Zmei (laki-laki, змей) dan zmeya (perempuan), yang berarti "ular", adalah bentuk naga dalam dongeng dan epos Rusia, kadang tokoh mirip manusia bersifat naga.
claims.quote: meaning "serpent", is a form of dragon in Russian folktales and epic poetry; sometimes, a human-like character with dragon-like traits.

claims.statement: The two most famous zmei, Gorynych and Tugarin, appear as adversaries of the bogatyrs Dobrynya Nikitich or Alyosha Popovich.
claims.statement_id: Dua zmei paling terkenal adalah Gorynych dan Tugarin, lawan para bogatyr Dobrynya Nikitich atau Alyosha Popovich.
claims.quote: Two of the most famous zmei are Gorynych and Tugarin, two well-known zmei, appear as adversaries of the bogatyri (heroes) Dobrynya Nikitich or Alyosha Popovich.

claims.statement: Another form is zmiy, borrowed from Church Slavonic.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk lain adalah zmiy, serapan dari bahasa Slavonik Gereja.
claims.quote: Another form is zmiy (змий, zmij), borrowed from Church Slavonic

claims.statement: Despite meaning serpent, when used of dragons zmei always implies the flying kind all over Russia.
claims.statement_id: Walau berarti ular, bila merujuk naga istilah zmei di seluruh Rusia selalu menyiratkan jenis yang terbang.
claims.quote: Despite meaning serpent, when referring to dragons, the term zmei always implicitly refers to the flying kind all over Russia.

claims.statement: Zmey Gorynych is a Russian folk dragon who abducts women; he usually lives in the mountains, often by a fiery river, guarding the Kalinov Bridge to the realm of the dead.
claims.statement_id: Zmey Gorynych adalah naga cerita rakyat Rusia yang menculik perempuan; ia biasanya tinggal di pegunungan, sering dekat sungai api, dan menjaga Jembatan Kalinov menuju alam orang mati.
claims.quote: Змей Горы́ныч — русский фольклорный змей (дракон), похищающий женщин. Змей Горыныч обитает обычно в горах, нередко у огненной реки и стережёт «Калинов мост», по которому попадают в царство мёртвых.

claims.statement: Many heads are the Zmey's constant trait, usually multiples of three (3, 6, 9, 12); most often three-headed; he usually flies but his wings are rarely mentioned; in Afanasyev's whole collection "fiery wings" appear only once.
claims.statement_id: Kepala banyak adalah ciri tetap Zmey, biasanya kelipatan tiga (3, 6, 9, 12); paling sering berkepala tiga; umumnya dapat terbang tetapi sayapnya jarang disebut; dalam seluruh kumpulan dongeng Afanasyev "sayap api" hanya disebut sekali.
claims.quote: Многоголовость Змея — непременная его черта. Число голов обычно кратно трём, чаще всего их бывает 3, 6, 9 или 12 ... Чаще всего Змей предстаёт трёхглавым. ... В большинстве случаев у Змея отмечается способность к полёту, но о крыльях его, как правило, ничего не говорится. Так, во всём сборнике русских народных сказок Александра Афанасьева лишь один раз сообщается об «огненных крыльях»

claims.statement: Indrik (the Indrik-Beast) of the Dove Book and Russian folklore is a fabulous beast, king of all animals, living on "the Holy Mountain" where no other foot may tread; when it stirs the earth trembles.
claims.statement_id: Indrik (Binatang Indrik) dalam Kitab Merpati dan cerita rakyat Rusia adalah binatang dongeng, raja segala binatang, yang tinggal di "Gunung Suci" yang tak boleh diinjak kaki lain; bila bergerak, bumi bergetar.
claims.quote: is a fabulous beast, the king of all animals, who lives on a mountain known as "The Holy Mountain" where no other foot may tread. When it stirs, the Earth trembles.

claims.statement: It is described as a gigantic bull with deer legs, a horse head and an enormous horn on its snout, vaguely like a rhinoceros.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai banteng raksasa berkaki rusa, berkepala kuda, dan bercula besar di moncong, agak mirip badak.
claims.quote: It is described as a gigantic bull with legs of a deer, the head of a horse and an enormous horn in its snout, making it vaguely similar to a rhinoceros.

claims.statement: The word "Indrik" is a distorted version of the Russian word for unicorn (yedinorog).
claims.statement_id: Kata "Indrik" adalah bentuk terdistorsi dari kata Rusia untuk unicorn (yedinorog).
claims.quote: The word "Indrik" is a distorted version of the Russian word for unicorn

claims.statement: Indrik in Russian legends is an animal, "father of all beasts", a character of the Dove Book.
claims.statement_id: Indrik (Индрик) dalam legenda Rusia adalah binatang "bapak segala binatang", tokoh Kitab Merpati.
claims.quote: И́ндрик (Индрик-зверь) — в русских легендах животное, «всем зверям отец», персонаж «Голубиной книги».

claims.statement: The beast's image is thought to reflect the mythological mammoth, a large underground animal in the myths of Siberia and the Far East.
claims.statement_id: Diduga gambaran Indrik mencerminkan mamut mitologis, binatang besar dalam mitologi Siberia dan Timur Jauh yang hidup di bawah tanah.
claims.quote: Предположительно, в образе мифического зверя отражены представления о мифологическом мамонте, крупном животном из мифологии народов Сибири и Дальнего Востока, обитающем под землёй

claims.statement: In physiologus and azbukovnik texts it is a horned hybrid with a horse's head and tail and a fish's body.
claims.statement_id: Dalam naskah fisiolog dan azbukovnik ia digambarkan sebagai binatang bertanduk campuran berkepala dan berekor kuda dan bertubuh ikan.
claims.quote: В «физиологах» и «азбуковниках» представлен как рогатое животное гибридной природы (голова и хвост коня, тело рыбы).

claims.statement: The Russian folk creature gives its name to Indricotherium, a synonym of Paraceratherium, the biggest land mammal ever.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk cerita rakyat Rusia ini memberi nama pada Indricotherium, sinonim Paraceratherium, mamalia darat terbesar yang pernah hidup.
claims.quote: The Russian folkloric creature gives its name to a synonym of Paraceratherium, Indricotherium, the biggest land mammal ever to live.

claims.statement: Likho (Polish licho) embodies evil fate and misfortune in Slavic mythology, a one-eyed creature often shown as a skinny old woman in black (One-eyed Likho) or an evil male forest goblin.
claims.statement_id: Likho (Лихо, Polandia licho) adalah perwujudan nasib buruk dan kemalangan dalam mitologi Slavia, makhluk bermata satu yang sering digambarkan sebagai perempuan tua kurus berpakaian hitam (Likho Bermata Satu) atau goblin hutan laki-laki yang jahat.
claims.quote: is an embodiment of evil fate and misfortune in Slavic mythology. A creature with one eye who is often depicted as an old, skinny woman in black (Лихо одноглазое, One-eyed Likho) or as an evil male goblin of forests.

claims.statement: Likho is traditionally found in fairy tales rather than the major canon of Slavic belief.
claims.statement_id: Likho secara tradisional ditemukan dalam dongeng, bukan dalam kanon utama kepercayaan Slavia.
claims.quote: Rather than being included in the major canon of the Slavic belief system, the Likho is traditionally found in fairy tales.

claims.statement: Likho cheats a person and rides on their neck; wanting to drown it, the person jumps into a river and drowns, while Likho floats away after other victims.
claims.statement_id: Likho menipu seseorang dan menunggang di lehernya; orang yang ingin menenggelamkannya melompat ke sungai dan malah tenggelam, sementara Likho mengapung keluar untuk mengejar korban lain.
claims.quote: Likho cheats a person and rides on their neck. The person wanting to drown Likho jumps into a river and drowns themself, but Likho floats out to chase other victims.

claims.statement: In superstition Likho was supposed to come and eat a person, used especially to scare small children; there are also tales of a person finally cheating Likho.
claims.statement_id: Dalam takhayul, Likho dikatakan datang dan memakan orang, dan ini dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak kecil; ada juga kisah manusia yang akhirnya menipu Likho.
claims.quote: Within the framework of superstitions, Likho was supposed to come and eat a person. In particular, this was used to scare small children.

claims.statement: In Russian likho means "evil, misfortune", originally "leftover, superfluous"; in tales Likho is often linked with Gore (Grief) and brings all kinds of misfortune to those it is near.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Rusia, likho berarti "kejahatan, kemalangan", dengan makna asal "sisa, berlebih"; dalam dongeng Likho sering dikaitkan dengan Gore (Duka) dan membawa berbagai kemalangan kepada orang yang didekatinya.
claims.quote: Лихо в русском языке — «зло, несчастье», в первоначальном значении — «остаточный, лишний».

claims.statement: In the Russian folk tale "One-eyed Likho" it appears as a thin, one-eyed, man-eating giantess.
claims.statement_id: Dalam dongeng rakyat Rusia "Likho Bermata Satu", Likho tampil sebagai raksasa perempuan kurus bermata satu pemakan manusia.
claims.quote: В русской народной сказке «Лихо одноглазое» предстаёт в образе худой одноглазой великанши-людоедки.

claims.statement: Likho is not a real proper name but a noun meaning bad luck in modern Russian and Ukrainian.
claims.statement_id: Likho bukan nama diri, melainkan kata benda yang berarti nasib buruk dalam bahasa Rusia dan Ukraina modern.
claims.quote: Likho is not a real proper name but a noun meaning bad luck in modern Russian and Ukrainian

claims.statement: Ördög (Ürdüng in Old Hungarian) is a shape-shifting demonic creature of Hungarian mythology and early paganism who controls the dark and evil forces of the world.
claims.statement_id: Ördög (Ürdüng dalam bahasa Hungaria Kuno) adalah makhluk iblis pengubah wujud dari mitologi dan paganisme awal Hungaria yang menguasai kekuatan gelap dan jahat di dunia.
claims.quote: (Ürdüng in Old Hungarian) is a shape-shifting, demonic creature from Hungarian mythology and early Hungarian paganism who controls the dark and evil forces of the world.

claims.statement: After Christianisation it was identified with the Devil; in Hungarian mythology God (Isten) had Ördög's help in creating the world.
claims.statement_id: Setelah Kristenisasi ia disamakan dengan Iblis; dalam mitologi Hungaria Tuhan (Isten) dibantu Ördög saat menciptakan dunia.
claims.quote: After Christianization, it was identified with the devil. In Hungarian mythology God (Isten in Hungarian) had help from Ördög when creating the world.

claims.statement: Ördög looks somewhat like a satyr or faun, man above and goat below, usually pitch-black, with cloven hooves, ram-like horns, a long blade-tipped tail, carrying a pitchfork.
claims.statement_id: Ördög agak mirip satir atau faun, bertubuh atas lelaki dan bawah kambing, biasanya hitam pekat, berkuku belah, bertanduk domba, berekor panjang berujung bilah, dan membawa garpu.
claims.quote: Ördög looks somewhat like a satyr or faun, a humanoid with the upper torso of a human male and lower portions of a goat; usually pitch-black, with cloven hooves, ram-like horns, a long tail ending in a blade; and he carries a pitchfork.

claims.statement: He dwells in the underworld or hell (Pokol), constantly stirring a huge cauldron of sinners' souls; it is uncertain, however, whether the underworld was a place of punishment in pre-Christian Hungarian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Ia tinggal di dunia bawah atau neraka (Pokol), terus mengaduk kuali besar berisi jiwa orang berdosa; namun tidak pasti apakah dunia bawah dianggap tempat hukuman dalam mitologi Hungaria pra-Kristen.
claims.quote: He dwells in the underworld or hell (Pokol in Hungarian), constantly stirring a huge cauldron filled with souls of those who lived in sin (however, it is uncertain whether the underworld was regarded as place of punishment or not in pre-Christian Hungarian mythology

claims.statement: In other legends, on earth he becomes a fox, a dark flame or a Hungarian shepherd with dark, sparkling eyes; he habitually bets with humans to see if they become corrupted, aiming to collect souls; other legends have him hide in victims' walls.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda lain, saat ke bumi ia menjelma rubah, nyala api gelap, atau gembala Hungaria bermata gelap berkilat; ia biasa bertaruh dengan manusia untuk melihat apakah mereka menjadi rusak, dengan tujuan mengumpulkan jiwa; menurut legenda lain ia bersembunyi di dinding rumah korban.
claims.quote: In other legends, when he comes to earth, he takes the form of a fox, a dark flame or a Hungarian shepherd with dark, sparkling eyes. It is his habit to make bets with humans to see if they become corrupted. His long-term goal is to collect more human souls

claims.statement: According to some legends, when he comes to earth he hides in victims' walls and makes faint, shrill, squeaky sounds.
claims.statement_id: Menurut beberapa legenda, saat datang ke bumi ia bersembunyi di dinding rumah korban dan mengeluarkan bunyi halus yang melengking.
claims.quote: Когда он всё-таки приходит на землю, то, согласно некоторым легендам, он прячется в стенах жертв и издаёт едва уловимые звуки, звучащие пронзительно и даже пискляво.

claims.statement: In Slavic mythology a vedmak is a warlock or male witch, the female equivalent being the vedma; the role stresses the shamanic side of Slavic paganism: treating people and animals, yet thought linked to the devil and able to harm by sickness, killing cattle or spoiling harvests.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, vedmak adalah dukun atau penyihir laki-laki, padanan perempuannya vedma; peran ini menekankan sisi syamanistik paganisme Slavia: mengobati manusia dan hewan, tetapi juga dianggap terhubung dengan iblis dan mampu mencelakai dengan penyakit, membunuh ternak, atau merusak panen.
claims.quote: is a warlock or male witch, the female equivalent (witch) being vedma. This role greatly focuses on the Shamanic aspects of Slavic paganism.

claims.statement: The vedmak is a figure of Slavic mythology and demonology, a sorcerer heading the witches of a district, who may side with them or protect people from witches and restless dead, healing people and animals with charms.
claims.statement_id: Vedmak (Ведьмак, Polandia wiedźmak) adalah tokoh mitologi dan demonologi Slavia, seorang penyihir, pemimpin para penyihir di suatu daerah, yang bisa bekerja sama dengan mereka atau melindungi orang dari ulah mereka dan dari arwah penasaran, serta menyembuhkan penyakit manusia dan hewan dengan mantra.
claims.quote: персонаж славянской мифологии и демонологии, колдун. Является начальником над ведьмами определённой местности; может действовать заодно с ними или, наоборот, защищать людей от проделок ведьм и заложных покойников, заговорами лечить болезни людей и животных.

claims.statement: A vedmak can turn into any animal or object.
claims.statement_id: Vedmak dapat berubah menjadi binatang atau benda apa pun.
claims.quote: A vedmak can turn into any animal or any object.

claims.statement: By belief a vedmak, like other sorcerers, may be "born" or "taught"; a born vedmak may lack beard and moustache but have a small tail.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan, vedmak seperti penyihir lain bisa "terlahir" atau "terlatih"; vedmak yang terlahir mungkin tak berjanggut dan berkumis, tetapi memiliki ekor kecil.
claims.quote: По поверьям, ведьмак, как и другие колдуны, может быть «прирождённым» или «наученным». У «прирождённого» ведьмака может не быть бороды, усов, зато присутствует маленький хвостик

claims.statement: Vedmak stems from Proto-Slavic *vědět ("to know") and Old East Slavic вѣдь ("knowledge; witchcraft").
claims.statement_id: Kata vedmak berasal dari Proto-Slavia *vědět ("mengetahui") dan Slavia Timur Kuno вѣдь ("pengetahuan; ilmu sihir").
claims.quote: Vedmak stems from Proto-Slavic *vědět ("to know") and Old East Slavic вѣдь ("knowledge; witchcraft"

claims.statement: Under the influence of Andrzej Sapkowski's fantasy saga The Witcher, vedmak is sometimes rendered as "witcher" in English.
claims.statement_id: Karena pengaruh saga fantasi The Witcher karya Andrzej Sapkowski, istilah vedmak kadang diterjemahkan sebagai "witcher" dalam bahasa Inggris.
claims.quote: Under the influence of The Witcher fantasy saga by Andrzej Sapkowski, the term vedmak is sometimes also rendered as "witcher" in English in certain contexts.

claims.statement: With his magic powers a vedmak can turn at will into a moth, horse, wolf or other animals.
claims.statement_id: Dengan kemampuan sihirnya, vedmak dapat sesuka hati berubah menjadi ngengat, kuda, serigala, atau binatang lain.
claims.quote: Обладая магическими способностями, ведьмак может по своему усмотрению оборачиваться мотыльком, конём, волком или другими животными.

claims.statement: Berehynia, perhaps the same as perehenia, is a being of East Slavic mythology, a lesser spirit related to rusalki; the name is linked to riverbanks and hills; in the few fragmentary mentions berehyni appear only in the plural and their look and functions are unknown.
claims.statement_id: Berehynia (Берегиня), mungkin sama dengan perehenia, adalah makhluk mitologi Slavia Timur, roh rendah yang berkerabat dengan rusalka; namanya dikaitkan dengan tepi sungai dan bukit; dalam sedikit sumber kuno ia hanya muncul dalam bentuk jamak dan wujud serta fungsinya tidak diketahui.
claims.quote: (можливо, тотожна переге́ні) — істота східнослов'янської міфології, нижчий дух, споріднений із русалками. Ім'я духа пов'язують з берегами й «перегинами»-пагорбами. У лічених фрагментарних згадках берегині фігурують виключно в множині; їхній вигляд, риси і точні функції невідомі.

claims.statement: The popular modern neo-mythological construct of Berehynia as an ancient Ukrainian pagan goddess has no historical, ethnographic or archaeological basis.
claims.statement_id: Konstruksi neomitologis populer modern tentang Berehynia sebagai dewi pagan Ukraina kuno tidak punya dasar sejarah, etnografi, maupun arkeologi.
claims.quote: Сучасний популярний неоміфологічний конструкт Берегині як давньоукраїнської язичницької богині не має історичного, етнографічного та археологічного підґрунтя.

claims.statement: Practically nothing is known from ancient sources about the berehyni's traits or activities, as only their name is mentioned.
claims.statement_id: Dari sumber kuno hampir tidak diketahui apa ciri dan tugas berehynia, karena sumber itu hanya menyebut namanya.
claims.quote: Зі стародавніх джерел невідомо практично нічого про те, які особливі риси та заняття притаманні берегиням, оскільки в таких джерелах згадується лише їхня назва.

claims.statement: In the late 20th century (XX), Ukrainian romantic nationalism focused on this matriarchal myth.
claims.statement_id: Pada akhir abad ke-20 (XX), nasionalisme romantis Ukraina memusatkan perhatian pada mitos matriarkal ini.
claims.quote: À la fin du XXe siècle, le nationalisme romantique ukrainien s’est concentré sur ce mythe matriarcal.

claims.statement: Most academic researchers consider the image of the "ancient Ukrainian goddess Berehynia" a pseudoscientific product of romantic literature; since about the 1980s berehyni have been read as female spirits guarding home and family.
claims.statement_id: Kebanyakan akademisi menganggap gambaran "dewi Ukraina kuno Berehynia" sebagai produk pseudoilmiah karya sastra romantis; sejak sekitar 1980-an berehynia ditafsirkan sebagai roh perempuan penjaga rumah dan keluarga.
claims.quote: Більшість академічних дослідників вважають образ «давньоукраїнської богині Берегині» псевдонауковим продуктом літературної романтичної творчості.

claims.statement: Some researchers considered berehyni close to rusalki, that is, drowned girls or girls who died unbaptised.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian peneliti menganggap berehynia dekat dengan rusalka, yaitu gadis yang mati tenggelam atau meninggal sebelum dibaptis.
claims.quote: Деякі дослідники вважали берегинь наближеними до русалок. Тобто, берегині — це утоплениці чи померлі нехрещеними дівчатка.

claims.statement: The Brosno dragon (Brosnya) is a supposed lake monster said in Russian folklore to inhabit Lake Brosno near Andreapol in western Russia, described as dragon-like and the subject of regional legends, some said to date to the 13th century.
claims.statement_id: Naga Brosno (Brosnya, Бросня) adalah monster danau yang menurut cerita rakyat Rusia menghuni Danau Brosno dekat Andreapol di Rusia barat, digambarkan mirip naga, dan menjadi pokok sejumlah legenda daerah yang sebagian disebut berasal dari abad ke-13.
claims.quote: is a supposed lake monster which in Russian folklore is said to inhabit Lake Brosno near Andreapol in western Russia. It is described as resembling a dragon and is the subject of a number of regional legends, some which are said to date back to the 13th century.

claims.statement: In the 18th and 19th centuries it was rumoured that the giant creature surfaced in the evening but dived at once when people approached.
claims.statement_id: Pada abad ke-18 dan ke-19 beredar kabar bahwa makhluk raksasa itu muncul ke permukaan danau pada senja hari tetapi segera menyelam bila orang mendekat.
claims.quote: It was rumored in the 18th and 19th centuries that the giant creature emerged to the lake's surface in the evening, but immediately submerged when people approached.

claims.statement: It is said that during World War II the beast swallowed a German aeroplane.
claims.statement_id: Konon pada Perang Dunia II binatang itu menelan sebuah pesawat Jerman.
claims.quote: It is said that during World War II the beast swallowed up a German airplane.

claims.statement: Many are sceptical about Brosnya and suggest it may be a beaver or a giant pike.
claims.statement_id: Banyak orang meragukan keberadaan Brosnya dan menduga makhluk itu berang-berang atau ikan tombak raksasa.
claims.quote: Many people treat the existence of Brosnya skeptically and say that the creature may be a beaver or a giant pike.

claims.statement: According to legends and many local accounts, Lake Brosno is the home of a "dragon", a mythical animal; locals periodically say they saw a large lizard or heard "it breathing under water".
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda dan banyak pernyataan penduduk setempat, Danau Brosno adalah tempat tinggal "naga", binatang mitis; penduduk kadang mengaku melihat kadal besar atau mendengar "ia bernapas di bawah air".
claims.quote: Согласно легендам и многочисленным заявлениям местных жителей, озеро Бросно — место обитания «дракона», мифического животного. Местные жители периодически говорят, что видели большого ящера или слышали, «как он дышит под водой».

claims.statement: Such legends most likely arose from the lake's unusual depth and remoteness from large settlements; in addition, decay at depth produces hydrogen-sulphide "bubbles" rising to the surface.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini kemungkinan besar muncul karena danau itu sangat dalam dan jauh dari permukiman besar; selain itu pembusukan di dasar danau menghasilkan gelembung hidrogen sulfida yang naik ke permukaan.
claims.quote: Причиной возникновения подобных легенд, скорее всего, стала необычно большая глубина озера и удалённость его от крупных населённых пунктов. Кроме того, процессы гниения, происходящие на глубине, приводят к образованию сероводородных «пузырей», выходящих на поверхность.

claims.statement: The kulshedra or kuçedra is a water, storm, fire and chthonic demon of Albanian myth, usually a huge many-headed female serpent-dragon; archetype of darkness and evil opposing the drangue; believed to spit fire and cause drought, storms, floods, earthquakes and other disasters.
claims.statement_id: Kulshedra atau kuçedra adalah iblis air, badai, api, dan dunia bawah dalam mitologi Albania, biasanya naga ular betina raksasa berkepala banyak; arketipe kegelapan dan kejahatan, lawan drangue; dipercaya menyemburkan api dan menimbulkan kekeringan, badai, banjir, gempa, dan bencana lain.
claims.quote: is a water, storm, fire and chthonic demon in Albanian mythology and folklore, usually described as a huge multi-headed female serpentine dragon. She is the archetype of darkness  and evil, the complementary and opposing force to drangue ... The kulshedra is believed to spit fire, cause drought, storms, flooding, earthquakes and other natural disasters against mankind.

claims.statement: In Albanian mythology she is usually fought and defeated by a drangue, a winged divine protector of mankind; heavy thunderstorms are thought to result from their battles; other sky heroes such as E Bija e Hënës dhe e Diellit also fight her.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Albania ia biasanya dilawan dan dikalahkan drangue, pahlawan ilahi bersayap pelindung manusia; badai petir besar dianggap akibat pertempuran mereka; ia juga dilawan pahlawan langit lain seperti E Bija e Hënës dhe e Diellit.
claims.quote: In Albanian mythology she is usually fought and defeated by a drangue, who is a semi-human winged divine hero and protector of mankind, the most widespread Albanian culture hero. Heavy thunderstorms are thought to be the result of most of their battles.

claims.statement: Kuçedër (kuçedra) derives from Latin chersydrus (from Greek), roughly "amphibious snake".
claims.statement_id: Kuçedër (kuçedra) berasal dari bahasa Latin chersydrus (dari bahasa Yunani), yang kira-kira berarti "ular amfibi".
claims.quote: or kuçedër (def. kuçedra) derives from the Latin chersydrus (from Greek χέρσυδρος) roughly meaning an "amphibious snake".

claims.statement: In folk belief the kulshedra's earlier stage is the bolla, a demonic chthonic-aquatic serpent whose eyes stay shut all year except on Saint George's Day; if it lives the set years unseen by humans it becomes a kulshedra.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat, tahap awal kulshedra adalah bolla, ular iblis bersifat dunia bawah dan air yang matanya tertutup sepanjang tahun kecuali pada Hari Santo Georgius; bila hidup bertahun-tahun tanpa terlihat manusia, bolla berubah menjadi kulshedra.
claims.quote: According to folk beliefs, the kulshedra's earlier stage is the bolla, which takes the form of demonic serpent possessing both chthonic and aquatic attributes. The bolla's eyes remain shut for the whole year except on Saint George's Day ... The bolla will eventually develop into a kulshedra if it should manage to live for the prescribed number of years without being seen by a human.

claims.statement: The kulshedra can also appear disguised as a woman hiding her true nature.
claims.statement_id: Kulshedra juga bisa muncul menyamar sebagai perempuan yang menyembunyikan sifat aslinya.
claims.quote: The kulshedra can also appear disguised as a woman, who keeps her true nature hidden

claims.statement: The kulshedra is generally a female dragon like a many-headed serpent with drooping breasts touching the ground, red woolly hair, a long tail and seven to twelve heads.
claims.statement_id: Kulshedra umumnya dianggap naga betina berwujud ular berkepala banyak dengan payudara menjuntai sampai ke tanah, berbulu merah, berekor panjang, dan berkepala tujuh sampai dua belas.
claims.quote: Kulshedra is generally considered to be a female dragon, like a multi-headed serpent form, but it is known to have pendulous drooping breasts touching the ground

claims.statement: The village where the kulshedra lives is said to prosper in farming and livestock, as her breath absorbs foodstuffs from everywhere, while other villages grow poor.
claims.statement_id: Desa tempat kulshedra tinggal dikatakan makmur dalam pertanian dan ternak, karena napasnya menyerap bahan makanan dari mana-mana, sementara desa lain menjadi miskin.
claims.quote: It is said that the village where the kulshedra lives has great prosperity in agriculture and livestock. Indeed, she absorbs by her breath foodstuffs from everywhere, and her village thrives, while the affected villages become poor and do not prosper.

claims.statement: Kuçedra or kulshedra is a mythological figure of Albanian folk tales and myths imagined as a great snake with 7 or 12 heads, or a many-headed legged dragon who usually seized water springs and ate people approaching them.
claims.statement_id: Kuçedra atau kulshedra adalah tokoh mitologis dongeng dan mitos rakyat Albania yang dibayangkan sebagai ular besar berkepala 7 atau 12 (tujuh, dua belas), atau naga berkepala banyak berkaki yang biasanya menguasai mata air dan memakan orang yang mendekat.
claims.quote: Kuçedra ose kulshedra është një figurë mitologjike e përrallave dhe miteve popullore shqiptare që përfytyrohej herë si një gjarpër i madh me 7 ose 12 koka, apo një dragua me shumë koka e me këmbë që zakonisht zinte burimet e ujit dhe hante njerëzit që i afroheshin burimeve.

claims.statement: Potrimpo (also Potrimpus, Autrimpo, Natrimpe) was a god of seas, earth, grain and crops in pagan Baltic and Prussian mythology, one of the three main Old Prussian gods; most knowledge comes from unreliable 16th-century sources.
claims.statement_id: Potrimpo (juga Potrimpus, Autrimpo, Natrimpe) adalah dewa laut, bumi, gandum, dan tanaman dalam mitologi pagan Baltik dan Prusia, salah satu dari tiga dewa utama Prusia Kuno; pengetahuan tentangnya kebanyakan dari sumber abad ke-16 yang kurang andal.
claims.quote: (also Potrimpus, Autrimpo, Natrimpe) was a god of seas, earth, grain, and crops in the pagan Baltic, and Prussian mythology. He was one of the three main gods worshiped by the Old Prussians. Most of what is known about this god is derived from unreliable 16th-century sources.

claims.statement: He was first mentioned (as Natrimpe) in the 1418 memorandum Collatio Episcopi Varmiensis from the Bishop of Warmia to Pope Martin V.
claims.statement_id: Ia pertama kali disebut (sebagai Natrimpe) dalam memorandum Collatio Episcopi Varmiensis tahun 1418 dari Uskup Warmia kepada Paus Martinus V.
claims.quote: He was first mentioned (as Natrimpe) in a 1418 memorandum Collatio Espiscopi Varmiensis sent by the Bishop of Warmia to Pope Martin V.

claims.statement: Simon Grunau claimed Potrimpo was a grain god forming a pagan trinity with thunder god Perkūnas and death god Peckols; he was depicted as a merry youth wearing a wreath of grain ears, and snakes, as his creatures, were worshipped and given milk.
claims.statement_id: Simon Grunau menyebut Potrimpo dewa gandum yang bersama dewa guntur Perkūnas dan dewa kematian Peckols membentuk tritunggal pagan; ia digambarkan sebagai pemuda riang berkalung untaian bulir gandum, dan ular sebagai makhluknya dipuja serta diberi susu.
claims.quote: Simon Grunau claimed that Potrimpo was a god of grain and together with thunder god Perkūnas and death god Peckols formed a pagan trinity. He was depicted on the purported Flag of Widewuto as a young, merry man wearing a wreath of grain ears. Grunau further claimed that snakes, as creatures of Potrimpo, were worshipped and given milk

claims.statement: The Sudovian Book (1520–1530) listed Potrimpo as god of running water and Autrimpo as god of the seas.
claims.statement_id: Kitab Sudovia (1520–1530) menyebut Potrimpo sebagai dewa air mengalir dan Autrimpo sebagai dewa laut.
claims.quote: The Sudovian Book (1520–1530) listed Potrimpo (Potrimpus) as god of running water and Autrimpo (Autrimpus) as god of the seas.

claims.statement: Later authors copied these descriptions, often merging Potrimpo and Autrimpo into one deity of earth and water.
claims.statement_id: Penulis kemudian menyalin uraian ini dan sering menggabungkan Potrimpo dan Autrimpo menjadi satu dewa bumi dan air.
claims.quote: Later authors copied these descriptions, often merging Potrimpo and Autrimpo into one deity of earth and water.

claims.statement: Patrimps (Potrimpus) in Baltic mythology is a water god, a god of magic in serpent form, ruler of life, fertility and death.
claims.statement_id: Patrimps (Potrimpus) dalam mitologi Baltik adalah dewa air, dewa sihir berwujud ular, penguasa kehidupan, kesuburan, dan kematian.
claims.quote: w mitologii bałtyjskiej bóg wody, bóg magii w postaci węża. Władca życia, płodności i śmierci.

claims.statement: The strzyga (plural strzygi, male strzygoń; sometimes striga) is usually a female demon of Slavic mythology stemming from the Strix of ancient Rome and Greece, vampire-like, found mainly in Polish and Silesian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Strzyga (jamak strzygi, laki-laki strzygoń; kadang diterjemahkan striga) biasanya iblis perempuan dalam mitologi Slavia yang berasal dari Strix Romawi dan Yunani kuno, mirip vampir, dan terutama ditemukan dalam cerita rakyat Polandia dan Silesia.
claims.quote: is usually a female demon in Slavic mythology, which stems from the mythological Strix of ancient Rome and ancient Greece. The demon is similar to a vampire, and is predominantly found in Polish and Silesian folklore.

claims.statement: According to Aleksander Brückner the word derives from strix, Latin for owl and a bird-like creature feeding on human flesh and blood in Roman and Greek myth; Hungarian sztriga, Albanian shtriga and Romanian strigă are cognate.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Aleksander Brückner, kata ini berasal dari strix, bahasa Latin untuk burung hantu dan makhluk mirip burung pemakan daging dan darah manusia dalam mitologi Romawi dan Yunani; kata Hungaria sztriga, Albania shtriga, dan Rumania strigă berkerabat.
claims.quote: According to Aleksander Brückner, the word is derived from Strix, Latin for owl and a bird-like creature which fed on human flesh and blood in Roman and Greek mythology. Hungarian sztriga, the Albanian shtriga and Romanian: strigă are also cognate and related.

claims.statement: The strzyga remained popular in rural Polish folklore into the late 19th and early 20th century, as Władysław Reymont showed in his Nobel Prize-winning novel Chłopi (The Peasants).
claims.statement_id: Strzyga tetap populer dalam cerita rakyat pedesaan Polandia hingga akhir abad ke-19 dan awal abad ke-20, seperti ditunjukkan Władysław Reymont dalam novel Chłopi (Para Petani) yang meraih Hadiah Nobel.
claims.quote: The strzyga remained a popular element in the folklore of rural Poland well into the late 19th and early 20th century, as shown by Władysław Reymont in his Nobel Prize-winning novel Chłopi (The Peasants).

claims.statement: After the 18th century strzyga and upiór were distinguished: the first tied more to witchcraft, the second more a flying vampiric creature.
claims.statement_id: Setelah abad ke-18 dibedakan antara strzyga dan upiór: yang pertama lebih terkait sihir, yang kedua lebih berupa makhluk vampir yang terbang.
claims.quote: After the 18th century, there was a distinction between strzyga and upiór; the first one was more connected to witchcraft, while the latter was more of a flying, vampiric creature.

claims.statement: To stop a strzyga harming people she was dug up and her heart pierced with an oak stake, or her head cut off; someone suspected of becoming one was buried face down with a stone under the lips.
claims.statement_id: Agar strzyga (Стрыга) tidak mencelakai orang, makamnya digali dan jantungnya ditusuk pasak kayu ek, atau kepalanya dipenggal; orang yang dicurigai akan menjadi strzyga dikuburkan telungkup dengan batu di bawah bibirnya.
claims.quote: Чтобы стрыга не могла вредить людям, нужно было выкопать её и проколоть ей сердце дубовым колышком ... либо отрезать ей голову и затем ударить её по ногам. Если кого-то при жизни могли заподозрить, что после смерти он станет стрыгой, то его хоронили ртом вниз и вставляли ему под губы камень

claims.statement: In Silesian belief a person was born a strzyga; in life she has two hearts, two souls and two rows of teeth; babies born with developed teeth were sometimes taken for strzygi; after death one soul leaves and the other lives on in the body in the coffin.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan Silesia, strzyga lahir sebagai strzyga; semasa hidup ia punya dua hati, dua jiwa, dan dua baris gigi; bayi yang lahir dengan gigi kadang disangka strzyga; setelah mati satu jiwa pergi dan yang lain tetap hidup di dalam jasad di peti.
claims.quote: В отличие от вампиров, стрыгоем, согласно силезским поверьям, человек рождался сразу. При жизни стрыга имеет два сердца, две души и два ряда зубов ... Известны случаи, когда за стрыг принимали младенцев, рождавшихся с развитыми зубами. Считалось, что после смерти стрыги одна душа покидала тело, а другая оставалась в нём и продолжала жить в теле в гробу

claims.statement: Strzygi were also sometimes depicted as owls living in dark forests.
claims.statement_id: Strzyga kadang juga digambarkan sebagai burung hantu yang tinggal di hutan gelap.
claims.quote: Стрыги также изображались иногда и как совы, обитающие в тёмных лесах

claims.statement: Svyatogor (also Sviatogor) is a mythical bogatyr in Russian byliny (oral epic poems); his name derives from the words for "sacred mountain".
claims.statement_id: Svyatogor (Святогор, juga Sviatogor) adalah bogatyr mitis dalam bylina (puisi epos lisan) Rusia; namanya berasal dari kata untuk "gunung suci".
claims.quote: is a mythical bogatyr (knight-errant) in Russian byliny (oral epic poems). His name derives from the words for "sacred mountain".

claims.statement: According to the epic, Mother Earth cannot support Svyatogor's weight, but he cannot overcome the "pull of the earth" in the bag; trying to lift it, his feet sink into the ground.
claims.statement_id: Menurut epos, Ibu Bumi tak sanggup menahan berat Svyatogor, tetapi ia tak mampu mengatasi "tarikan bumi" dalam kantong; ketika mencoba mengangkatnya, kakinya terbenam ke tanah.
claims.quote: According to the epic, Mother Earth cannot support the weight of Svyatogor, but he cannot overcome the "pull of the earth" contained in the bag; when he tries to lift the bag, his feet sink into the ground.

claims.statement: Svyatogor and Ilya Muromets come to a giant stone coffin and both sense it is for Svyatogor; it is too big for Ilya but fits Svyatogor perfectly, and when he closes the lid it seals.
claims.statement_id: Svyatogor dan Ilya Muromets tiba di peti mati batu raksasa dan sama-sama merasa peti itu untuk Svyatogor; peti itu terlalu besar untuk Ilya tetapi pas untuk Svyatogor, dan ketika ia menutupnya, peti itu tersegel.
claims.quote: They arrive at a giant stone coffin and both have a premonition that it is for Svyatogor. Ilya manages to lie down in the coffin first, but it appears too large for him, but it fits Svyatogor perfectly. When Svyatogor closes the lid, it seals the coffin.

claims.statement: In old Russian mythology Svyatogor is a giant bogatyr, among the oldest heroes of the Russian bylina epic, outside the Kiev and Novgorod cycles.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Rusia kuno Svyatogor adalah bogatyr raksasa, salah satu pahlawan tertua epos bylina Rusia di luar siklus Kiev dan Novgorod.
claims.quote: в древнерусской мифологии богатырь-великан. Относится к наиболее древним героям русского былинного эпоса, находящегося вне киевского и новгородского циклов

claims.statement: Svyatogor is a huge giant "taller than the standing forest, lower than the walking cloud", living on the high Holy Mountains; when he rides Mother Earth shakes, forests sway and rivers overflow; he is the oldest Russian bogatyr, pre-Christian, divine and mighty.
claims.statement_id: Svyatogor adalah raksasa "lebih tinggi dari hutan yang berdiri, lebih rendah dari awan yang berjalan", tinggal di Pegunungan Suci yang tinggi; bila ia berkuda Ibu Bumi berguncang, hutan bergoyang, dan sungai meluap; ia bogatyr Rusia tertua, pra-Kristen, ilahi, dan perkasa.
claims.quote: Святогор в эпосе является огромным великаном, «выше леса стоячего, ниже облака ходячего». Он не ездит на Святую Русь, а живёт на высоких Святых горах; при его поездке Мать — Сыра Земля потрясается, леса колышутся и реки выливаются из берегов. Святогор является русским древнейшим богатырём, дохристианским, божественным и могучим.

claims.statement: Before dying Svyatogor passes part of his strength to Ilya with his breath.
claims.statement_id: Sebelum mati Svyatogor mewariskan sebagian kekuatannya kepada Ilya lewat napasnya.
claims.quote: Перед смертью Святогор с дыханием передаёт Илье часть своей силы.

claims.statement: Babay is a night spirit (bogeyman) of Slavic folklore who abducts children who do not sleep or behave badly; also called Babayka, Babayko (Ukrainian) or Bobo (Polish).
claims.statement_id: Babay (Бабай) adalah roh malam (momok) dalam cerita rakyat Slavia yang menculik anak yang tidak tidur atau nakal; juga disebut Babayka, Babayko (Ukraina), atau Bobo (Polandia).
claims.quote: is a night spirit (Bogeyman) in Slavic folklore. According to beliefs, he abducts children who do not sleep at night or behave badly. He is also called Babayka (Russian: Бабайка), Babayko (Ukrainian: Бабайко) or Bobo (Babok, Bebok) (Polish)

claims.statement: Babay is rarely described so children imagine their worst form, but sometimes he is a pitch-black crooked old man with defects like muteness, armlessness or lameness, carrying a bag and cane; he lives in the forest, a swamp or a garden.
claims.statement_id: Babay jarang digambarkan agar anak membayangkannya dalam wujud paling menakutkan, tetapi kadang ia lelaki tua hitam bengkok dengan cacat seperti bisu, tak berlengan, atau pincang, membawa karung dan tongkat; ia tinggal di hutan, rawa, atau kebun.
claims.quote: Babay is rarely described, so that children can imagine him in the form most terrible for them, but sometimes Babay is described as a pitch-black and crooked old man. He has some physical defects, such as muteness, armlessness, and/or lameness. He has a bag and a cane.

claims.statement: At night he roams the streets and bags anyone he meets; he stands by windows watching children, and sometimes hides under a child's bed and may take them if they get up.
claims.statement_id: Pada malam hari ia berkeliling jalan dan memasukkan orang yang ditemuinya ke dalam karung; ia berdiri di dekat jendela mengawasi anak-anak, dan kadang bersembunyi di bawah tempat tidur anak serta mengambilnya bila anak itu bangun.
claims.quote: At night, he wanders through the streets and puts into his bag those who meet him on the way. Walking near houses, Babay stands close to the windows and watches the children. ... Also, Babay can sometimes hide under the child's bed, and he may take them if they're awake or get up.

claims.statement: The term babay, with its synonym baba, is most likely Turkic, translated from Tatar as "grandfather" or "old man".
claims.statement_id: Kata babay, bersama sinonimnya baba, kemungkinan besar berasal dari bahasa Turkik dan dari bahasa Tatar diterjemahkan "kakek" atau "lelaki tua".
claims.quote: The term babay, alongside its synonym, baba, is most likely of Turkic origin. It is translated as "grandfather", "old man" from the Tatar language.

claims.statement: In Polish folk belief the bobo was a small, ugly, spiteful being used to frighten children into discipline.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Polandia, bobo adalah makhluk kecil, buruk rupa, dan jahat yang dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak agar disiplin.
claims.quote: W polskich wierzeniach ludowych bobo był małą, brzydką i złośliwą istotą, którą straszono dzieci w celu ich zdyscyplinowania.

claims.statement: The bobo is mentioned in the early 17th-century (XVII) Peregrynacja dziadowska, which says it beat children and did damage in the house.
claims.statement_id: Bobo disebut dalam Peregrynacja dziadowska dari awal abad ke-17 (XVII), yang menyatakan bobo memukul anak-anak dan merusak rumah.
claims.quote: Wzmianka o bobie znajduje się w pochodzącej z początku XVII wieku Peregrynacji dziadowskiej – według niej bobo miał bić dzieci i czynić w domu różne szkody.

claims.statement: The bauk is an animal-like mythical creature of Serbian mythology hiding in dark places, holes or abandoned houses, waiting to grab, carry off and devour its victim, but scared away by light and noise.
claims.statement_id: Bauk (Баук) adalah makhluk mitis mirip binatang dalam mitologi Serbia yang bersembunyi di tempat gelap, lubang, atau rumah kosong, menunggu untuk menyergap, membawa pergi, dan melahap korbannya, tetapi dapat diusir dengan cahaya dan bunyi.
claims.quote: is an animal-like mythical creature in Serbian mythology. The bauk is described as hiding in dark places, holes, or abandoned houses, waiting to grab, carry away, and devour its victim; but it can be scared away by light and noise.

claims.statement: Interpreting the bauk's traits suggests it is really a description of actual bears, already extinct in parts of Serbia and known only as legend.
claims.statement_id: Penafsiran sifat-sifat bauk mengarah pada kesimpulan bahwa ia sebenarnya gambaran beruang sungguhan yang di sebagian Serbia sudah punah dan hanya dikenal sebagai legenda.
claims.quote: Interpretation of the bauk's attributes leads to the conclusion that the bauk is actually a description of real bears, which were already regionally extinct in some parts of Serbia and known only as legend.

claims.statement: The word bauk was originally used as a hypocorism for the bear.
claims.statement_id: Kata bauk semula dipakai sebagai hipokorisme (sebutan sayang) untuk beruang.
claims.quote: Сама ријеч баук је првобитно била коришћена као хипокоризам за медвједа.

claims.statement: The bauk is a being of South Slavic mythology, especially Serbian, once used to frighten small children.
claims.statement_id: Bauk adalah makhluk mitologi Slavia Selatan, terutama dalam mitologi Serbia, yang dulu dipakai untuk menakut-nakuti anak kecil.
claims.quote: Баук је биће из митологије Јужних Словена, које је нарочито заступљено у митологији Срба. Са њиме су се некада плашила мала дјеца.

claims.statement: The verb bauljati, meaning a clumsy walk, comes from this creature's name; its onomatopoeia is "bau" and its euphemism baja.
claims.statement_id: Kata kerja bauljati, yang berarti berjalan canggung, berasal dari nama makhluk ini; bunyi tiruannya "bau", dan eufemismenya baja.
claims.quote: Глагол бауљати, која означава неспретан ход, долази од имена овог митолошког бића. Ономатопеја која се користи за ријеч баук је бау, а еуфемизам ове ријечи је баја.

claims.statement: Bauk is used to translate goblin in Serbian editions of J. R. R. Tolkien's works.
claims.statement_id: Bauk dipakai untuk menerjemahkan goblin dalam edisi Serbia karya J. R. R. Tolkien.
claims.quote: Bauk is used as the translation for goblin in Serbian editions of works of J. R. R. Tolkien

claims.statement: In the reveal trailer for The Witcher IV by CD Projekt Red, protagonist Ciri is seen fighting a bauk.
claims.statement_id: Dalam trailer gim The Witcher IV dari CD Projekt Red, tokoh utama Ciri tampak melawan bauk.
claims.quote: In the cinematic reveal trailer for the upcoming video game The Witcher IV by Polish developer CD Projekt Red, the game's main protagonist Ciri can be seen fighting a bauk.

claims.statement: Ileana Cosânzeana is a figure of Romanian mythology, shown as a beautiful, good-natured princess or emperor's daughter, or as a fairy of immense power.
claims.statement_id: Ileana Cosânzeana adalah tokoh mitologi Rumania, digambarkan sebagai putri cantik dan baik hati atau putri seorang kaisar, atau sebagai peri yang sangat sakti.
claims.quote: is a figure in Romanian mythology. She is represented as a beautiful and good-natured princess or daughter of an Emperor, or described as a fairy with immense powers.

claims.statement: According to Nina Cuciuc her name is also written Cosînzeana, Sânziana and Ileana Cosînzeana Sora Soarelui ("Sister of the Sun"), and she is called "Queen of Flowers".
claims.statement_id: Menurut Nina Cuciuc, namanya juga ditulis Cosînzeana, Sânziana, dan Ileana Cosînzeana Sora Soarelui ("Saudari Matahari"), dan ia disebut "Ratu Bunga".
claims.quote: According to professor Nina Cuciuc, her name can also be translated or written as the following: Cosînzeana, Cosenzeana, Sânziana, Sînziana, Ileana Kossinzana, Hélène Cossinzana and Ileana Cosînzeana Sora Soarelui ("Sister of the Sun"). She can also be described as "Queen of Flowers".

claims.statement: According to Adela Ileana Draucean, Ileana derives from Elena, and cosânzeana is linked to sânziană, a Romanian holiday and another term for fairies.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Adela Ileana Draucean, nama Ileana berasal dari Elena, dan cosânzeana berkaitan dengan sânziană, hari raya Rumania dan sebutan lain bagi peri.
claims.quote: According to Adela Ileana Draucean, the name Ileana derives from Elena, and cosânzeana is linked to sânziană, a Romanian holiday and another term to designate fairies in Romanian mythology.

claims.statement: Romanian linguist Sorin Paliga lists other names: Ileana Simziana, Floarea Florilor ("the Flower of Flowers") and Frumoasa lumii ("the Beauty of the World").
claims.statement_id: Ahli bahasa Rumania Sorin Paliga mencatat nama lain: Ileana Simziana, Floarea Florilor ("Bunga segala Bunga"), dan Frumoasa lumii ("Kecantikan Dunia").
claims.quote: Romanian linguist Sorin Paliga also lists several alternate names for the character: Ileana Simziana, Floarea Florilor ("the Flower of Flowers"); Frumoasa lumii ("The Beauty of the World")

claims.statement: Folklorist Lazar Saineanu rendered her name in French as Hélène aux cheveux d'or ("Helen with Golden Hair").
claims.statement_id: Folkloris Lazăr Șăineanu (Lazar Saineanu) menerjemahkan namanya ke bahasa Prancis sebagai Hélène aux cheveux d'or ("Helena Berambut Emas").
claims.quote: El folclorista Lazar Saineanu tradujo su nombre al francés como Hélène aux cheveux d'or (sic) ("Helena de cabello dorado")

claims.statement: She is shown as a beautiful, kind princess or emperor's daughter, or as a fairy of immense power.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai putri cantik dan baik hati atau putri kaisar, atau sebagai peri yang sangat sakti.
claims.quote: Se la representa como una bella y bondadosa princesa o hija de un emperador,  o se la describe como un hada con inmensos poderes.

claims.statement: In Slavic mythology the Raróg or Raróh is a fire demon, often depicted as a fiery falcon.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, Raróg (Рарог) atau Raróh adalah iblis api yang sering digambarkan sebagai elang api.
claims.quote: In Slavic mythology, the Raróg (Russian: Рарог) or Raróh (Ukrainian: Рарог) is a fire demon, often depicted as a fiery falcon.

claims.statement: In Czech folklore a raroh can hatch from an egg incubated on a stove for nine days and nights and appear as a fiery falcon or dragon; in Polish folklore the rarog is a tiny pocket-sized bird bringing happiness.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat Ceko, raroh dapat menetas dari telur yang dierami di atas tungku selama sembilan hari dan malam, dan tampil sebagai elang api atau naga; dalam cerita rakyat Polandia raróg adalah burung mungil yang muat di saku dan membawa kebahagiaan.
claims.quote: According to Czech folklore, a raroh can hatch from an egg that was incubated on a stove for nine days and nights, and can appear either as a fiery falcon or a dragon. In Polish folklore, the rarog is a tiny bird that can be held in a pocket, and can bring people happiness.

claims.statement: Proto-Slavic *rarogъ, "falcon, hawk" (?), goes back to Proto-Indo-European.
claims.statement_id: Kata Proto-Slavia *rarogъ, "elang, alap-alap" (?), berakar pada bahasa Proto-Indo-Eropa.
claims.quote: Праславянское *rarogъ (*warogъ?) «сокол, ястреб» (?) восходит к праиндоевропейскому

claims.statement: A caldera on Jupiter's moon Io was named Rarog Patera.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kaldera di bulan Io milik Jupiter dinamai Rarog Patera.
claims.quote: A caldera on Jupiter's moon Io was named Rarog Patera

claims.statement: In Slavic mythology the Raróg is a fire spirit tied to the hearth cult, pictured as a bird (usually of prey) or a dragon with a sparkling body, or a fiery whirlwind.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Slavia Raróg adalah roh api yang terkait pemujaan perapian, dibayangkan sebagai burung (biasanya pemangsa) atau naga bertubuh berpercikan, juga sebagai pusaran api.
claims.quote: в славянской мифологии огненный дух, связанный с культом очага. Рарога представляли в образе птицы (обычно хищной) или дракона с искрящимся телом, а также в виде огненного вихря.

claims.statement: The rarášek is credited with turning into various birds and beasts.
claims.statement_id: Rarášek dikatakan mampu berubah menjadi berbagai burung dan binatang.
claims.quote: Рарашку приписывается способность превращаться в различных птиц и зверей.

claims.statement: If the rarášek is hostile to a person, it scatters all their unharvested grain to dust.
claims.statement_id: Bila Rarášek memusuhi seseorang, ia menghancurkan seluruh gandumnya yang belum dipanen menjadi debu.
claims.quote: Если Рарашек враждебен человеку, он разносит и обращает в прах весь его несжатый хлеб.

claims.statement: The samodiva (plural samodivi), samovila or vila are fairies, wood nymphs or harmful female demons of South and West Slavic folklore.
claims.statement_id: Samodiva (самодива, jamak samodivi), samovila, atau vila adalah peri, nimfa hutan, atau iblis perempuan berbahaya dalam cerita rakyat Slavia Selatan dan Barat.
claims.quote: are fairies, wood nymphs, or harmful female demons found in South and West Slavic folklore.

claims.statement: They are beautiful women with long blonde or red hair in white dresses, with veils, wreaths or green sashes giving them supernatural power or flight, sometimes winged; a recurring theme is a man robbing a samodiva of her veil or wreath to capture her and force her to be his bride.
claims.statement_id: Mereka perempuan cantik berambut panjang pirang atau merah, berbaju putih dengan kerudung, karangan bunga, atau selempang hijau yang memberi kekuatan gaib atau kemampuan terbang, kadang bersayap; tema berulang: lelaki mencuri kerudung atau karangan bunga samodiva untuk menangkapnya dan memaksanya menjadi pengantin.
claims.quote: They are described as beautiful women with long flowing tresses of blonde or red hair. They wear white dresses and various other articles of clothing (white veils, wreathes, green sash) said to confer them their supernatural powers (or ability to fly); ... able to rob a samodiva of her veil, wreathe, etc. to capture her, and force her to become his bride

claims.statement: Their secret home is on heights, by water or in woodland, usually combined, such as a mountain spring or a beech grove by a lake where they bathe.
claims.statement_id: Kediaman rahasia mereka berada di tempat tinggi, dekat perairan, atau hutan, biasanya gabungan, misalnya mata air di gunung atau hutan beech di tepi danau tempat mereka mandi.
claims.quote: Their secret home occurs at a place associated with high elevation, or bodies of water, or woodland, usually in combination, e.g. a spring on a mountain, or a beechwood grove by a lake where they bathe

claims.statement: Superstition warns against trespassing on their territory, especially to draw water at night; the trespasser may be struck with illness, death or other suffering.
claims.statement_id: Takhayul memperingatkan agar orang tidak melanggar wilayah mereka, terutama menimba air pada malam hari; pelanggar bisa ditimpa sakit, maut, atau penderitaan lain.
claims.quote: Superstition cautions that one should fear trespassing upon their territory, particularly to draw water at night, and the encroacher may be stricken with illness, death, or some other suffering as consequence.

claims.statement: Samodivas were the souls of beautiful women living in hard-to-reach caves by springs, wastelands or abandoned windmills.
claims.statement_id: Samodiva adalah jiwa perempuan cantik yang tinggal di gua sulit dijangkau dekat mata air, padang sunyi, atau kincir angin kosong.
claims.quote: Były to dusze pięknych kobiet, zamieszkujące trudno dostępne pieczary przy źródłach wodnych, pustkowia czy opuszczone wiatraki

claims.statement: The samodiva is a demon of Bulgarian folklore, like the vile and yudy, related to rusalki.
claims.statement_id: Samodiva adalah iblis cerita rakyat Bulgaria, mirip vila dan yuda, berkerabat dengan rusalka.
claims.quote: Samodiwa, samowiła, wiła – demon folkloru bułgarskiego, podobny do wił i jud, pokrewny rusałkom.

claims.statement: At night they washed their white garments, dried them in the moonlight and guarded them jealously, for all their power lay in them, then bathed and sang and danced the hora in a nearby glade.
claims.statement_id: Malam hari mereka mencuci baju putih, mengeringkannya di bawah cahaya bulan dan menjaganya agar tak dicuri karena di situlah seluruh kekuatan mereka, lalu mandi dan menari hora di padang terbuka.
claims.quote: rozbierały się do naga, prały swoje białe szaty, suszyły w blasku księżyca, zazdrośnie ich strzegły, aby nie zostały ukradzione, bowiem w nich tkwiła cała ich moc. Następnie kąpały się, później na polanie obok śpiewały i tańczyły horę.

claims.statement: Samodivas also appeared as women working at harvest and helped young couples with children, but mostly they were unfriendly to people, stopping springs.
claims.statement_id: Samodiva juga muncul sebagai perempuan yang bekerja saat panen dan membantu pasangan muda beranak, tetapi kebanyakan tidak ramah kepada manusia, misalnya menahan mata air.
claims.quote: Samodiwy pojawiały się także jako pracujące kobiety przy zbiorach, wspierały młode małżeństwa z dziećmi. W większości przypadków były jednak nieprzyjazne dla ludzi – wstrzymywały źródła

claims.statement: The upiór is a demonic being of Slavic and Turkic folklore, a prototype of the vampire; belief in the ubır (upiór) is suggested to have spread across the Eurasian steppes with the Kipchak-Cuman migrations, originating around the Volga and the Pontic steppes.
claims.statement_id: Upiór adalah makhluk iblis dari cerita rakyat Slavia dan Turkik, cikal bakal vampir; diduga kepercayaan akan ubır (upiór) menyebar melintasi stepa Eurasia lewat migrasi Kipchak-Kuman, setelah berasal dari sekitar Sungai Volga dan stepa Pontus.
claims.quote: is a demonic being from Slavic and Turkic folklore, a prototype of the vampire. It is suggested that the ubır (upiór) belief spread across the Eurasian steppes through the migrations of the Kipchak-Cuman people, after having its origins in the regions surrounding the Volga (İtil) River and the Pontic steppes.

claims.statement: The modern word "vampire" derives from the Old Slavic and Turkic form onpyr, with "v-" added before a nasal vowel, a feature of Old Bulgarian.
claims.statement_id: Kata modern "vampir" berasal dari bentuk Slavia Kuno dan Turkik onpyr, dengan tambahan bunyi "v-" sebelum vokal sengau, ciri bahasa Bulgaria Kuno.
claims.quote: The modern word "vampire" derives from the Old Slavic and Turkic form "онпыр" (onpyr), with the addition of the sound "v-" before a large nasal vowel (on), characteristic of Old Bulgarian

claims.statement: Names of the upiór across languages: Tatar Ubır, Turkish Ubır or Obur, Belarusian vupyr, Bulgarian văpir, Serbian vampir, Czech and Slovak upír, Polish upiór, Russian upyr', Ukrainian upyr.
claims.statement_id: Nama upiór dalam berbagai bahasa: Tatar Ubır, Turki Ubır atau Obur, Belarus vupyr, Bulgaria văpir, Serbia vampir, Ceko dan Slovakia upír, Polandia upiór, Rusia upyr', Ukraina upyr.
claims.quote: (lengua tártara: Убыр (Ubır), turco: Ubır, Obur, Obır, (bielorruso moderno: вупыр (vupyr), búlgaro: въпир (văpir), serbio: вампир ( vampir ), checo y eslovaco: upír, Polaco: upiór, wupi, Ruso: упырь (upyr'), ucraniano: упир (upyr)

claims.statement: Slavs believed that at death the soul leaves the body and wanders its neighbourhood and workplace for 40 days before going to the afterlife; during this time it could re-enter the corpse.
claims.statement_id: Bangsa Slavia percaya saat mati jiwa keluar dari tubuh dan berkeliaran di sekitar rumah dan tempat kerjanya selama 40 hari sebelum ke alam baka; selama itu jiwa dapat masuk kembali ke jasad.
claims.quote: The Slavs believed that upon death the soul would go out of the body and wander about its neighbourhood and workplace for 40 days before moving on to an eternal afterlife.

claims.statement: A vampire is an unclean spirit possessing a decomposing body; this undead creature needs the blood of the living and is vengeful and envious toward them.
claims.statement_id: Vampir adalah perwujudan roh najis yang merasuki jasad yang membusuk; makhluk mayat hidup ini membutuhkan darah orang hidup dan dianggap pendendam serta iri kepada mereka.
claims.quote: A vampire is the manifestation of an unclean spirit possessing a decomposing body. This undead creature needs the blood of the living to sustain its body's existence and is considered to be vengeful and envious towards the living.

claims.statement: The death of an unbaptised child, a violent or untimely death, or the death of a grave sinner (sorcerer, murderer) could make a soul unclean.
claims.statement_id: Kematian anak yang belum dibaptis, kematian karena kekerasan atau sebelum waktunya, atau kematian pendosa berat (penyihir, pembunuh) dapat membuat jiwa menjadi najis.
claims.quote: The death of an unbaptized child, a violent or an untimely death, or the death of a grievous sinner (such as a sorcerer or murderer) were all grounds for a soul to become unclean after death.

claims.statement: In Slavic folk culture the upiór has features strongly present in the strzyga.
claims.statement_id: Dalam budaya rakyat Slavia, upiór punya ciri yang juga kuat pada strzyga.
claims.quote: In Slavic folk culture, the upiór has features that are strongly present in strzyga

claims.statement: By popular belief the Witches of Anaga were women devoted to covens in the Anaga mountains in north-eastern Tenerife (Canary Islands, Spain).
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan populer, Penyihir Anaga adalah perempuan yang mengabdi pada perkumpulan sihir di pegunungan Anaga di timur laut Pulau Tenerife (Kepulauan Canaria, Spanyol).
claims.quote: were (according to popular belief) women who were devoted to covens in the mountainous area of Anaga in the northeast of the island of Tenerife (Canary Islands, Spain).

claims.statement: The rituals were held on the Anaga ridge between San Andrés and Taganana, at a place called El Bailadero after the witches' bonfire dances; afterwards they were believed to go down to the coast to swim naked.
claims.statement_id: Ritual diadakan di punggung pegunungan Anaga antara San Andrés dan Taganana, di tempat bernama El Bailadero yang merujuk tarian penyihir mengelilingi api unggun; setelah itu mereka dipercaya turun ke pantai untuk berenang telanjang.
claims.quote: These rituals were held in an area in the mountains of Anaga in the dorsal between San Andrés and Taganana. The area is called "El Bailadero", which refers to the dances performed by witches around a bonfire. It was believed that after the covens, witches came down to the coast to swim naked.

claims.statement: Over time, through Eastern European vampire stories, the myth added blood-drinking, making them witch-vampires who sucked the blood of sleeping newborns in their cribs.
claims.statement_id: Lama-kelamaan, karena pengaruh kisah vampir Eropa Timur, mitos ini menambahkan unsur minum darah sehingga mereka menjadi penyihir-vampir yang mengisap darah bayi yang tidur di buaian.
claims.quote: With the passage of time, due to the influence of vampire stories in Eastern Europe, this led to the myth that witches incorporated the aspect of drinking blood, thus making them witch-vampires; typically tales were created that these witches sucked the blood of newborns as they slept in their cribs.

claims.statement: This element is shared with mythologies elsewhere in Spain, such as the guaxas of Asturias and the guajonas of Cantabria.
claims.statement_id: Unsur ini juga ada dalam mitologi tempat lain di Spanyol, seperti guaxa di Asturias dan guajona di Cantabria.
claims.quote: Este aspecto también es compartido en las mitologías de otros lugares de España, tales como las guaxas en Asturias y las guajonas en Cantabria.

claims.statement: A theory holds that the legend came from Guanche pagan rain rituals, which the Catholic Church considered witchcraft.
claims.statement_id: Ada teori bahwa legenda ini berasal dari ritual pagan bangsa Guanche untuk merayakan hujan, yang dianggap sihir oleh Gereja Katolik.
claims.quote: There is also a theory that the origin of this legend was from pagan rituals associated with rituals that celebrated guanches rain; these rituals were considered as an act of witchcraft by the Catholic Church.

claims.statement: According to Canarian popular belief, the witches of El Bailadero de Anaga were women holding covens in a mountainous area of north-eastern Tenerife.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan populer Canaria, penyihir El Bailadero di Anaga adalah perempuan yang mengadakan pertemuan sihir di pegunungan timur laut Tenerife.
claims.quote: Según las creencias populares canarias, las llamadas brujas del Bailadero de Anaga eran mujeres que se dedicaban a hacer aquelarres en una zona montañosa del noreste de la isla de Tenerife

claims.statement: The zmeu (plural zmei, feminine zmeoaică) is a fantastic creature of Romanian folklore and mythology.
claims.statement_id: Zmeu (jamak zmei, perempuan zmeoaică) adalah makhluk fantastis dalam cerita rakyat dan mitologi Rumania.
claims.quote: is a fantastic creature of Romanian folklore and Romanian mythology.

claims.statement: Though some sources call it a dragon, the zmeu is distinct for its human-like traits: legs, arms, making and using weapons, riding a horse and wishing to marry young girls; some commentators class it as a giant (ogre), a devil or a vampire.
claims.statement_id: Walau sebagian sumber menyebutnya naga, zmeu berbeda karena bersifat manusia: berkaki, berlengan, membuat dan memakai senjata, menunggang kuda, dan ingin menikahi gadis muda; ada pengulas yang menggolongkannya sebagai raksasa (ogre), iblis, atau vampir.
claims.quote: Though referred by some sources as a dragon, the zmeu is nevertheless distinct, because it usually has clear anthropomorphic traits: it is humanoid and has legs, arms, the ability to create and use artifacts such as weapons, and to ride a horse, and has the desire to marry young girls. There are commentators that class it as a giant (equivalent of an ogre), or a devil, or even a vampire.

claims.statement: In some stories the zmeu appears in the sky and spits fire or can change form; in others it has a magic gem on its head shining like the sun.
claims.statement_id: Dalam beberapa cerita zmeu muncul di langit dan menyemburkan api, atau dapat berubah wujud; dalam cerita lain ia punya batu permata ajaib di kepala yang bersinar seperti matahari.
claims.quote: In some stories, Zmeu appears in the sky and spits fire, or has the ability to change form. In other stories, it has a magical precious stone on its head that shines like the sun.

claims.statement: It likes beautiful young girls and kidnaps them, usually to marry them, and is almost always defeated by a daring prince or knight-errant.
claims.statement_id: Ia menyukai gadis muda yang cantik dan menculiknya, biasanya untuk dinikahi, dan hampir selalu dikalahkan pangeran atau kesatria pemberani.
claims.quote: It likes beautiful young girls, whom it kidnaps, usually for the purpose of marrying them. It is almost always defeated by a daring prince or knight-errant.

claims.statement: Most scholars agree the Romanian term zmeu derives from Slavic zmey.
claims.statement_id: Kebanyakan sarjana sepakat istilah Rumania zmeu berasal dari kata Slavia zmey.
claims.quote: Most scholars agree that the Romanian term zmeu derives from Slavic zmey.

claims.statement: In Romanian mythology the zmeu is a giant being with supernatural powers, the embodiment of evil, always defeated by the forces of good.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Rumania, zmeu adalah makhluk raksasa berkekuatan gaib, perwujudan kejahatan, yang selalu dikalahkan oleh kekuatan baik.
claims.quote: En la mitología rumana, un esmeuro o dracosmeu (en rumano zmeu) es un ser gigante con poderes sobrenaturales, encarnación del mal, pero que siempre es derrotado por las fuerzas del bien

claims.statement: In Romanian the word zmeu also means the kites children fly.
claims.statement_id: Kata zmeu dalam bahasa Rumania juga berarti layang-layang yang diterbangkan anak-anak.
claims.quote: La palabra también se refiere a las cometas que vuelan los niños dado que la palabra zmeu también significa cometa en rumano.

claims.statement: The zmeu has also been conflated with the dracu or the balaur dragon; various stories have it slain by a young prince like Prâslea cel voinic.
claims.statement_id: Zmeu juga dikacaukan dengan dracu atau naga jenis balaur; dalam berbagai cerita ia dibunuh pangeran muda seperti Prâslea cel voinic.
claims.quote: The zmeu has also been conflated with or confused with the dracu or with the balaur type dragon. ... like Prâslea cel voinic

claims.statement: Antero Vipunen is a giant of Finnish mythology and runic songs, buried underground and possessing very valuable spells and knowledge.
claims.statement_id: Antero Vipunen adalah raksasa dalam mitologi dan lagu rune Finlandia yang terkubur di bawah tanah dan menyimpan mantra serta pengetahuan yang sangat berharga.
claims.quote: is a giant who appears in Finnish mythology and runic songs. He is buried underground and possesses very valuable spells and knowledge.

claims.statement: Väinämöinen needs three magic words (luotteet) to finish his boat; inside Vipunen he builds a forge and hammers, hurting Vipunen, who spits him out and gives him the words.
claims.statement_id: Väinämöinen membutuhkan tiga kata ajaib (luotteet) untuk menyelesaikan perahunya; di dalam Vipunen ia membuat tempat tempa dan memukul-mukul hingga Vipunen kesakitan dan memuntahkannya sambil memberikan kata-kata yang dibutuhkan.
claims.quote: Väinämöinen requires three magic words or luotteet to finish creating his boat ... Inside Vipunen, Väinämöinen creates a forge and starts hammering, causing pain for Vipunen. He spits Väinämöinen out, giving him the words he needs.

claims.statement: According to Matti Kuusi, Lemminkäinen was likely the original protagonist rather than Väinämöinen.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Matti Kuusi, tokoh utama aslinya kemungkinan Lemminkäinen, bukan Väinämöinen.
claims.quote: According to Matti Kuusi, Lemminkäinen was likely the original protagonist instead of Väinämöinen.

claims.statement: In Balto-Finnic folk poetry Antero Vipunen is a dead man or giant lying underground, a tietäjä (wise sorcerer) holding valuable ancient spells or knowledge.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi rakyat Balto-Finnik, Antero Vipunen adalah orang mati atau raksasa yang berbaring di bawah tanah, seorang tietäjä (dukun bijak) pemilik mantra atau pengetahuan purba yang berharga.
claims.quote: on itämerensuomalaisessa kansanrunoudessa maan alla makaava vainaja tai jättiläinen; tietäjä, jolla on hallussaan arvokkaita ikiaikaisia loitsuja tai tietoja.

claims.statement: In Estonian vibu means a bow, so in Estonia Vipunen was understood as a skilled archer.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Estonia vibu berarti busur, sehingga di Estonia Vipunen dipahami sebagai pemanah ulung.
claims.quote: Viron kielessä vibu merkitsee jousipyssyä, joten Virossa Vipunen on käsitetty taitavaksi jousimieheksi.

claims.statement: Many versions call Vipunen a trapper, as his name suggests; a vipu is a kind of snare.
claims.statement_id: Dalam banyak versi Vipunen disebut pemasang jerat, sesuai namanya; vipu adalah sejenis alat jerat.
claims.quote: Useissa kertomuksen versioissa Vipusen mainitaan olevan ansastaja, kuten nimestä Vipunen voi päätellä. Vipu on eräänlainen ansalaite.

claims.statement: In Polish pagan mythology boginki (singular boginka) are female spirits or demons of wild nature (forest, field, mountains, water), often personifying natural forces; the word means "minor goddess" and may be translated "fairy" or "nymph"; imagined as ugly hags or pretty girls, usually naked, and usually evil.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi pagan Polandia, boginki (tunggal boginka) adalah roh atau iblis perempuan alam liar (hutan, ladang, gunung, perairan), sering perwujudan kekuatan alam; kata ini berarti "dewi kecil" dan dapat diterjemahkan peri atau nimfa; mereka dibayangkan sebagai nenek buruk rupa atau gadis cantik, biasanya telanjang, dan umumnya jahat.
claims.quote: boginki (singular: boginka) are female spirits or demons of wild nature: forest, field, mountains, or water (both of land and sea) and is often a personification of the forces of nature. The word literally means "minor goddess" in Polish and may be translated as "fairy" or "nymph". They were usually imagined as either ugly old hags or pretty young girls, usually naked. They are usually evil.

claims.statement: Some boginki are rusałka, vila, dziwożona, łaskotałka, mamuna or nawka, and the term came to be applied to any of them.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian boginki adalah rusałka, vila, dziwożona, łaskotałka, mamuna, atau nawka, dan istilah boginka mulai dipakai untuk semuanya.
claims.quote: Some boginki are rusałka, vila, dziwożona, łaskotałka, mamuna ... or nawka. The term "boginka" started to be applied to any of them.

claims.statement: Boginki (mamuny) can steal a human child and substitute it; the substitute is called boginiak, płonek, podrzutek or odmieniak ("changeling"); children with mental disabilities were often thought to be such.
claims.statement_id: Boginki (mamuny) dapat mencuri anak manusia dan menggantinya; anak pengganti itu disebut boginiak, płonek, podrzutek, atau odmieniak; anak dengan disabilitas mental sering dianggap anak pengganti.
claims.quote: Boginki (mamuny) can steal a human child and substitute them. Such substituted child is called boginiak, płonek , podrzutek,  or odmieniak ("changeling").  Often children with mental disabilities were thought to be such.

claims.statement: The boginka's main functions are pursuing women in childbirth and pregnant women, and stealing and swapping children.
claims.statement_id: Fungsi utama boginka adalah mengejar perempuan yang baru melahirkan dan perempuan hamil, serta menculik dan menukar bayi.
claims.quote: Главные функции богинки — преследование рожениц и беременных, похищение и подмена детей.

claims.statement: In Orava and Spiš belief the boginka is an evil, ugly being, tall and gawky, with an oversized head, swollen belly, crooked legs, black teeth and large breasts thrown back over the shoulder; boginki can also appear as cats, dogs or frogs.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan di Orava dan Spiš, boginka adalah makhluk jahat buruk rupa bertubuh tinggi canggung, berkepala besar, berperut buncit, berkaki bengkok, bergigi hitam, dan berpayudara besar yang disampirkan ke belakang bahu; boginki juga dapat muncul sebagai kucing, anjing, atau katak.
claims.quote: В поверьях Оравы, Спиша и особенно Замагурья богинка описывается как злое уродливое существо c высокой нескладной фигурой, непропорционально большой головой, вздутым животом, кривыми ногами, чёрными зубами, большими грудями, которые закидывались назад через плечо. Также богинки могут появляться в виде животных — кошек, собак, лягушек и др.

claims.statement: Women who died in childbirth, suicides and child-murderers were said to become boginki; they lived in marshes, lakes, rivers, forests and mountains and were met by the water washing cloths.
claims.statement_id: Perempuan yang mati saat melahirkan, bunuh diri, atau membunuh anaknya dipercaya menjadi boginka; boginki tinggal di rawa, danau, sungai, hutan, dan gunung, dan dijumpai di tepi air saat mencuci kain.
claims.quote: Boginki zamieszkiwały bagna, jeziora, rzeki, lasy i góry. Można je było spotkać nad wodą podczas prania chust drewnianymi kijankami. ... Boginkami miały stawać się kobiety zmarłe przy porodzie, samobójczynie i morderczynie dzieci.

claims.statement: Fiery serpents (Russian ognennyi zmei, Ukrainian vohnyanyy zmiy) are evil beings in Russian folklore, often shapeshifted demons or spirits.
claims.statement_id: Ular api (Rusia ognennyi zmei, Ukraina vohnyanyy zmiy) adalah makhluk jahat dalam cerita rakyat Rusia, sering iblis atau roh yang berubah wujud.
