claims.quote: among other names, are evil beings in Russian folklore, often shapeshifted demons or spirits.

claims.statement: In East Slavic tradition the fiery serpent generally resembles a fiery shaft ("fiery carrying pole"), a flaming broom or a glowing ball of blue fire throwing sparks in flight; this has been linked to bolides, shooting stars or meteorites.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Slavia Timur, ular api umumnya mirip batang menyala ("pikulan api"), sapu yang terbakar, atau bola api biru yang memercikkan bunga api saat terbang; hal ini dikaitkan dengan bola api meteor, bintang jatuh, atau meteorit.
claims.quote: In East Slavic tradition, the "fiery serpent" is said to generally resemble a fiery shaft (Russian: коромысло, "fiery carrying pole"), a flaming broom, or a glowing ball of blue fire, releasing sparks during its flight. This has been connected to the astronomical phenomena of bolides, shooting stars (meteors) or meteorites.

claims.statement: In Russia the ognennyi zmei is also called zmey lyubak, nalotnik ("raider"), nalot or letun ("flyer").
claims.statement_id: Di Rusia ular api juga disebut zmey lyubak, nalotnik ("penyerbu"), nalot, atau letun ("penerbang").
claims.quote: In Russia, the ognennyi zmei is also known as the zmey lyubak (змей-любак, 'serpent-lyubak'), nalotnik (налётник, 'raider'),  nalot (налёт, 'raid'), letun (летун, 'flyer')

claims.statement: In Ukraine the perelesnyk ("tempter") is a demon in the form of a fiery snake (meteor) that flies towards women.
claims.statement_id: Di Ukraina, perelesnyk ("penggoda") adalah iblis berwujud ular api (meteor) yang terbang menuju perempuan.
claims.quote: In the Ukraine, the perelesnyk (Перелесник, 'tempter, seducer'; var. perevésnyk переве́сник), aka pervonach (Первонач), is a demon in the form of a fiery snake (meteor) that flies towards women.

claims.statement: The fiery serpent has sexual relations with women, resulting in their illness and death, and has a double form: a fiery winged serpent in the air, a man on the ground.
claims.statement_id: Ular api (Огненный змей) menjalin hubungan seksual dengan perempuan, yang berakibat sakit dan kematian sang perempuan, dan berwujud ganda: di udara ular api bersayap, di bumi manusia.
claims.quote: вступает сексуальные отношения с женщинами, результатом чего является болезнь и смерть женщины, также обладает двойственным внешним обликом — в воздухе имеет вид огненного крылатого змея, на земле — человека.

claims.statement: The fiery serpent is a guise of a walking dead man who comes after death to his wife or beloved.
claims.statement_id: Ular api adalah perwujudan mayat berjalan yang setelah mati datang kepada istrinya atau perempuan yang dicintainya.
claims.quote: Огненный змей является ипостасью ходячего покойника, после смерти являющегося к своей жене или любимой им женщине.

claims.statement: In Armenian and Turkish folklore the Lake Van Monster (Turkish Van Gölü Canavarı, Armenian Vana lchi hresh) is a lake monster said to live in Lake Van in eastern Turkey.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Armenia dan Turki, Monster Danau Van (Turki Van Gölü Canavarı, Armenia Vana lchi hresh) adalah monster danau yang konon tinggal di Danau Van, Turki timur.
claims.quote: In Armenian and Turkish folklores, the Lake Van Monster (Turkish: Van Gölü Canavarı, Armenian: Վանա լճի հրեշ, romanized: Vana lchi hresh) is a lake monster said to live in Lake Van in eastern Turkey.

claims.statement: The Armenian chroniclers Movses Khorenatsi and Anania Shirakatsi wrote of vishaps (Armenian water dragons) in Lake Van; in myth the god Vahagn, the vishapakagh ("reaper of vishaps"), plunged into the lake to drag out any vishap large enough to devour the world.
claims.statement_id: Penulis kronik Armenia Movses Khorenatsi dan Anania Shirakatsi menulis tentang vishap (naga air mitologi Armenia) di Danau Van; menurut mitos dewa Vahagn, sang vishapakagh ("penuai vishap"), terjun ke danau untuk menyeret keluar vishap yang cukup besar untuk melahap dunia.
claims.quote: The Armenian chroniclers Movses Khorenatsi and Anania Shirakatsi wrote about vishaps (water dragons in Armenian mythology) living in Lake Van. According to the myth, the god Vahagn, the vishapakagh ("reaper of vishaps"), would plunge into Lake Van to drag out any vishap that had grown large enough to devour the world.

claims.statement: James Russell writes that into modern times Armenians of the Van basin called the lake's sudden storms vishap kami ("dragon wind").
claims.statement_id: James Russell menulis bahwa hingga zaman modern orang Armenia di lembah Van menyebut badai mendadak di danau itu vishap kami ("angin naga").
claims.quote: Russell writes that into the modern period, the Armenians of the Van basin would refer to the sudden storms that arise on the lake as vishap kami

claims.statement: The Ottoman newspaper Saadet of 29 April 1889 reported a creature had dragged a man into Lake Van; the Ottoman government sent an official scientific survey, which failed to spot it.
claims.statement_id: Surat kabar Utsmaniyah Saadet tanggal 29 April 1889 memberitakan makhluk yang konon menyeret seorang lelaki ke Danau Van; pemerintah Utsmaniyah mengirim tim survei ilmiah resmi yang tidak berhasil melihat binatang itu.
claims.quote: A story in the Ottoman newspaper Saadet from 29 April 1889 claimed that a creature had purportedly dragged a man into Lake Van. Following reports of the incident, the Ottoman government sent an official scientific survey group to the lake. The group ultimately failed to spot the alleged animal.

claims.statement: The Lake Van Monster (Turkish Van Gölü Canavarı) is a lake monster said to inhabit Lake Van in eastern Turkey.
claims.statement_id: Monster Danau Van (Turki: Van Gölü Canavarı) adalah monster danau yang konon menghuni Danau Van di Turki timur.
claims.quote: El monstruo del Lago Van (Turco: Van Gölü Canavarı) es un monstruo de lago que presuntamente habita en el Lago de Van en Turquía oriental.

claims.statement: James Russell considers this legend an Armenian adoption of Urartian myths about the god Teisheba fighting a water monster.
claims.statement_id: James Russell menganggap legenda ini adopsi Armenia atas mitos Urartu tentang pertarungan dewa Teisheba dengan monster air.
claims.quote: El académico James Russell considera que esta leyenda es una adopción Armenia de los mitos Urartianos respecto al combate del dios Teisheba con el monstruo acuático

claims.statement: Lempo is a demon of Finnish folklore and mythology linked to the names Lemmes, Lemmas, Lemmätär and Lemmetär ("Lady Love") and to love and fire; the -tär names are feminine, but Lempo has also been seen as a male demon.
claims.statement_id: Lempo adalah iblis dalam cerita rakyat dan mitologi Finlandia, dikaitkan dengan nama Lemmes, Lemmas, Lemmätär, dan Lemmetär ("Nyonya Cinta") serta tema cinta dan api; nama berakhiran -tär bersifat perempuan, tetapi Lempo kadang dipahami sebagai iblis laki-laki.
claims.quote: is a demon from Finnish folklore and mythology. Lempo has been connected to the names Lemmes, Lemmas, Lemmätär and Lemmetär ... as well as themes of love and fire. The -tär ending names are feminine, but Lempo has also been understood as a male demon in some instances.

claims.statement: Christfried Ganander called Lempo a flying evil spirit who forged evil flying arrows.
claims.statement_id: Christfried Ganander menyebut Lempo roh jahat yang terbang dan menempa panah-panah jahat yang terbang.
claims.quote: Christfried Ganander called Lempo a flying evil spirit who forged evil flying arrows

claims.statement: Matthias Castrén linked Lempo to lempi, "erotic love", and thought a love god could have become an evil god; Elias Lönnrot linked it to the Swedish slem, "lousy".
claims.statement_id: Matthias Castrén mengaitkan nama Lempo dengan lempi, "cinta erotis", dan menduga dewa cinta dapat berkembang menjadi dewa jahat; Elias Lönnrot mengaitkannya dengan kata Swedia slem, "buruk".
claims.quote: Matthias Castrén connected the name Lempo to the word lempi 'erotic love'. ... so Castrén thought a love god could have thus developed into an evil god. Elias Lönnrot connected the name to the Swedish word slem 'lousy'.

claims.statement: In old Finnish belief Lempo is a mythical being or god whom Christianity identified with the Devil.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan kuno Finlandia, Lempo adalah makhluk kepercayaan atau dewa yang oleh Kekristenan disamakan dengan Iblis.
claims.quote: Lempo on suomalaisessa muinaisuskossa uskomusolento tai jumala, jonka kristinusko samaisti paholaiseen.

claims.statement: In spells this lempi could be a wild, raging feeling, like lust roused by an evil witch.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mantra, lempi bisa menjadi perasaan liar yang mengamuk, seperti nafsu yang dibangkitkan penyihir jahat.
claims.quote: This lempi in spells could be a wild and raging feeling, like lust awoken by an evil witch

claims.statement: The mild curse "Lempo soikoon!" was originally an appeal to Lempo.
claims.statement_id: Umpatan ringan "Lempo soikoon!" semula adalah seruan kepada Lempo.
claims.quote: Lievä kirous ”Lempo soikoon!” on ollut alun perin vetoamista Lempoon

claims.statement: A moroi is a type of vampire or ghost in Romanian folklore; a female is a moroaică; in some versions it is a phantom of the dead leaving the grave to draw energy from the living.
claims.statement_id: Moroi adalah sejenis vampir atau hantu dalam cerita rakyat Rumania; moroi perempuan disebut moroaică; dalam beberapa versi moroi adalah arwah orang mati yang keluar dari kubur untuk menyerap tenaga orang hidup.
claims.quote: is a type of vampire or ghost in Romanian folklore. A female moroi is called a moroaică (pl. moroaice). In some versions, a moroi is a phantom of a dead person which leaves the grave to draw energy from the living.

claims.statement: Moroi are often associated with other Romanian figures such as the strigoi (another vampire), vârcolac or pricolici (werewolves), and their traits vary by source.
claims.statement_id: Moroi sering dikaitkan dengan tokoh lain cerita rakyat Rumania seperti strigoi (vampir lain), vârcolac, atau pricolici (manusia serigala), dan ciri-cirinya berbeda menurut sumber.
claims.quote: Moroi are often associated with other figures in Romanian folklore, such as strigoi (another type of vampire), vârcolac (werewolf), or pricolici (werewolf). As with most concepts in folklore, the exact characteristics ascribed to moroi are variable from source to source.

claims.statement: Moroi may also mean an infant who died unbaptised; the term's origin is unclear, but the Romanian Academy thinks it may come from Old Slavonic mora ("nightmare").
claims.statement_id: Moroi juga bisa berarti bayi yang mati sebelum dibaptis; asal istilahnya tidak jelas, tetapi Akademi Rumania menduga berasal dari kata Slavonik Kuno mora ("mimpi buruk").
claims.quote: It may also signify an infant who died before being baptized. The origins of the term "moroi" are unclear, but it is thought by the Romanian Academy to have possibly originated from the Old Slavonic word mora ("nightmare")

claims.statement: The moroi is a type of vampire in Romanian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Moroi (Морой) adalah sejenis vampir dalam mitologi Rumania.
claims.quote: Моро́й (рум. moroi) — разновидность вампира в румынской мифологии.

claims.statement: Folklore-based literature distinguishes moroi as living vampires from strigoi as vampires risen from the dead, though Romanian folklore does not always keep this distinction.
claims.statement_id: Sastra berbasis cerita rakyat membedakan moroi sebagai vampir hidup dan strigoi sebagai vampir yang bangkit dari kematian, walau perbedaan ini tidak selalu dipegang dalam cerita rakyat Rumania.
claims.quote: Литература, основанная на фольклоре, объясняет различие между мороем и другой разновидностью вампира — стригоем — так: морои являются живыми вампирами, а стригои — вампирами, восставшими из мёртвых. Хотя в румынском фольклоре это различие не всегда соблюдено.

claims.statement: It may be related to Old Slavonic mora, from the Proto-Indo-European root *mer-, "to harm".
claims.statement_id: Kata ini mungkin berkaitan dengan kata Slavonik Kuno mora, dari akar Proto-Indo-Eropa *mer-, "mencelakai".
claims.quote: Оно может быть связано со старославянским «мора», возникшим от праиндоевропейского корня *mer- (вредить).

claims.statement: Wlislocki reported a belief that the child of a woman impregnated by a nosferat (a kind of incubus-vampire) would be very ugly, thickly haired, and quickly become a moroi.
claims.statement_id: Wlislocki mencatat kepercayaan bahwa anak dari perempuan yang dihamili nosferat (semacam vampir-inkubus) akan sangat buruk rupa, berbulu lebat, dan cepat menjadi moroi.
claims.quote: Wlislocki reported a belief that the child of a woman impregnated by a nosferat (a sort of incubus-vampire) would be extremely ugly and covered with thick hair, very quickly becoming a moroi.

claims.statement: Moroi and strigoi appear as vampire clans in Richelle Mead's "Vampire Academy" books and the 2014 film of the first book.
claims.statement_id: Moroi dan strigoi disebut sebagai klan vampir dalam buku Richelle Mead "Vampire Academy" dan film adaptasi buku pertamanya tahun 2014.
claims.quote: Морои (а также стригои) упоминаются как клан вампиров в книгах Райчел Мид «Академия вампиров» и в экранизации первой книги в 2014 году

claims.statement: The žaltys (grass snake) is a household spirit of Lithuanian mythology, sacred animal of the sun goddess Saulė, guardian of the home and symbol of fertility; people kept it by the stove believing it brought good harvests and wealth; killing it brought misfortune; one found in a field was given milk.
claims.statement_id: Žaltys (ular rumput) adalah roh rumah dalam mitologi Lituania, binatang suci dewi matahari Saulė, penjaga rumah dan lambang kesuburan; orang memeliharanya di dekat tungku dan percaya ia membawa panen baik dan kekayaan; membunuhnya mendatangkan malapetaka; bila ditemukan di ladang ia diberi susu.
claims.quote: is a household spirit in Lithuanian mythology. It is a sacred animal of the sun goddess Saulė, and was considered a guardian of the home and a symbol of fertility. People used to keep it as a pet by the stove or other special area of the house, believing that it would bring good harvest and wealth. Killing the žaltys was said to bring great misfortunes upon the household.

claims.statement: There is a story of a young woman named Eglė who found a žaltys in her clothes after bathing in a lake; it offered to return them if she married it; she agreed, and the žaltys, Žilvinas, King of the Grass Snakes, became a handsome young man and her husband.
claims.statement_id: Ada kisah gadis bernama Eglė yang menemukan žaltys di pakaiannya setelah mandi di danau; ular itu berjanji mengembalikan pakaiannya bila ia mau menikahinya; Eglė setuju, dan žaltys itu, Žilvinas, Raja Ular Rumput, menjelma pemuda tampan menjadi suaminya.
claims.quote: There is a story of a young women named Eglė who found a žaltys in her clothes after she bathed in a lake. He spoke to her and said he would give her back her clothes if she married him. She eventually agreed, and later the žaltys, who was King of the Grass Snakes Žilvinas, would take the form of a handsome young man to become her husband.

claims.statement: He took her to his undersea home, where she became immortal as Queen of the Grass Snakes.
claims.statement_id: Ia membawa Eglė ke rumahnya di bawah laut, tempat Eglė menjadi abadi sebagai Ratu Ular Rumput.
claims.quote: He took her to his undersea home where she became immortal as Queen of the Grass Snakes.

claims.statement: The žaltys was considered a messenger of the gods and the Sun's favourite, so killing it was a crime; a Lithuanian proverb says "At the sight of a dead grass snake even the Sun weeps".
claims.statement_id: Žaltys dianggap utusan para dewa dan kesayangan Matahari, sehingga membunuhnya disamakan dengan kejahatan; pepatah Lituania berkata "Melihat ular rumput mati, Matahari pun menangis".
claims.quote: Жалтис считался посланцем богов, любимцем Солнца, потому убийство Жалтиса приравнивалось к преступлению. В литовском языке существует пословица: «При виде мёртвого ужа и Солнце плачет».

claims.statement: The žaltys (Latvian Zalktis) is a deity in the form of a grass snake in Latvian and Lithuanian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Žaltys (Latvia: Zalktis) adalah dewa berwujud ular rumput dalam mitologi Latvia dan Lituania.
claims.quote: божество в образе ужа в латышской и литовской мифологии.

claims.statement: The žaltys was considered a protector of livestock and compared with Piena Māte (the Milk Mother).
claims.statement_id: Žaltys dianggap pelindung ternak dan dibandingkan dengan Piena Māte (Ibu Susu).
claims.quote: Жальтис считался покровителем скота и сравнивается с Piena Māte (Молочная мать).

claims.statement: Blud in Slavic mythology is an evil being that causes disorientation and leads a person aimlessly round and round; the term also means illicit fornication, whose desire Slavic clerics said came from the Devil.
claims.statement_id: Blud (Блуд) dalam mitologi Slavia adalah roh jahat yang membuat orang kehilangan arah dan menuntunnya berputar-putar tanpa tujuan; istilah ini juga berarti perzinaan, yang hasratnya menurut rohaniwan Slavia berasal dari Iblis.
claims.quote: one of the Slavic fairies in Slavic mythology, is an evil-deity that causes disorientation and leads a person aimlessly around and round. The term also refers to illicit fornication, the desire for which Slavic clerics claimed to come from the Devil.

claims.statement: Blud is a figure of Slavic, including Ukrainian, mythology, a kind of unclean force that deceives travellers, makes them wander, leads them off the road and into danger.
claims.statement_id: Blud adalah tokoh mitologi Slavia, termasuk Ukraina, sejenis roh najis yang mengelabui pelancong, membuat mereka tersesat, menyimpang dari jalan, dan masuk ke bahaya.
claims.quote: Блуд — персонаж слов'янської міфології, зокрема й української, різновид нечистої сили, що вводить в оману подорожніх, змушує їх блукати, збиває зі шляху, заводить у небезпеку.

claims.statement: By legend the blud is an angel (servant of Satan) cast from heaven by God; the other angels became devils, forest and water spirits and other unclean beings on falling to earth, but the blud had not landed and hung in the air when God said "Amen".
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita, blud adalah malaikat (pelayan Setan) yang dibuang Tuhan dari surga; malaikat lain yang jatuh ke bumi menjadi setan, roh hutan, roh air, dan roh najis lain, tetapi blud belum sempat mendarat dan tergantung di udara saat Tuhan berkata "Amin".
claims.quote: За переказами, блуд — це скинутий Богом з неба янгол (слуга Сатани). Інші янголи стали чортами, лісовиками, водяниками та іншою нечистою силою, коли впали на землю. Блуд не встиг приземлитися та завис у повітрі після того, як Бог промовив «Амінь».

claims.statement: So the blud clings to any passer-by who touches it by chance, making them wander by clouding the mind, sending false visions or calling with a voice.
claims.statement_id: Karena itu blud menempel pada setiap orang yang tak sengaja menyentuhnya, membuatnya tersesat dengan menggelapkan pikiran, mengirim penglihatan palsu, atau memanggil dengan suara.
claims.quote: Відтак блуд чіпляється до кожного перехожого, який випадково доторкнеться до нього. Він змушує людину блукати, затьмарюючи розум, насилаючи оманливі видіння чи кличучи голосом.

issues.message: Mengusulkan tradisi baru: "Chukotko-Kamchatkan (Chukchi, Koryak, Itelmen) traditions".
Klaim ini tidak dirujuk bagian teks mana pun.

claims.statement: Kutkh (also Kutkha) is a Raven spirit revered by various indigenous peoples of the Russian Far East; in many legends a key creation figure, ancestor of mankind, mighty shaman and trickster; popular in Chukchi stories and central to Koryak and Itelmen mythology in Kamchatka.
claims.statement_id: Kutkh (juga Kutkha, Кутх) adalah roh Gagak yang dihormati berbagai masyarakat adat Timur Jauh Rusia; dalam banyak legenda ia tokoh kunci penciptaan, leluhur manusia, dukun sakti, dan penipu; populer dalam cerita orang Chukchi dan sentral dalam mitologi Koryak dan Itelmen di Kamchatka.
claims.quote: is a Raven spirit traditionally revered in various forms by various indigenous peoples of the Russian Far East. Kutkh appears in many legends: as a key figure in creation, as a fertile ancestor of mankind, as a mighty shaman and as a trickster. He is a popular subject of the animist stories of the Chukchi people and plays a central role in the mythology of the Koryaks and Itelmens of Kamchatka.

claims.statement: Regionally he is Kúrkil among the Chukchi and Kutq among the Itelmens.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan Chukchi ia disebut Kúrkil, di kalangan Itelmen Kutq.
claims.quote: Regionally, he is known as Kúrkil among the Chukchi; as Kutq among the Itelmens

claims.statement: In Koryak the name is often used in augmentative form (KutqÍnnaku and others) meaning "Big Kutkh", often translated "God".
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Koryak namanya sering dipakai dalam bentuk pembesar (KutqÍnnaku dan lain-lain) yang berarti "Kutkh Besar" dan sering diterjemahkan "Tuhan".
claims.quote: In Koryak, the name is employed commonly in its augmentative form, (KutqÍnnaku, KusqÍnnaku, KuyÍnnaku) all meaning "Big Kutkh" and often translated simply as "God".

claims.statement: Kutkh's tales come in many contradictory versions: in some a Creator makes him and he lets the dawn onto the earth by chipping away the stones around her; in others he creates himself.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Kutkh punya banyak versi yang sering bertentangan: dalam sebagian ia diciptakan Sang Pencipta dan membawa fajar ke bumi dengan memecahkan batu yang mengurungnya; dalam versi lain ia menciptakan dirinya sendiri.
claims.quote: The tales of Kutkh come in many, often contradictory versions. In some tales he is explicitly created by a Creator and lets the dawn onto the earth by chipping away at the stones surrounding her. In others he creates himself

claims.statement: Many Kutkh stories resemble Raven tales of the Pacific Northwest Coast peoples, suggesting long indirect cultural contact between Asia and North America.
claims.statement_id: Banyak kisah Kutkh mirip cerita Gagak masyarakat adat Pantai Barat Laut Pasifik, menunjukkan sejarah panjang kontak budaya tak langsung antara Asia dan Amerika Utara.
claims.quote: Many of the stories regarding Kutkh are similar to those of the Raven among the indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast, suggesting a long history of indirect cultural contact between Asian and North American peoples.

claims.statement: Kutkh or Kutkha is the embodiment of the Raven spirit traditionally revered by various indigenous peoples of the Russian Far East.
claims.statement_id: Kutkh atau Kutkha adalah perwujudan roh Gagak yang secara tradisional dihormati berbagai masyarakat adat di Timur Jauh Rusia.
claims.quote: Кутх или Кутха — воплощение духа Ворона, традиционно почитающееся различными коренными народностями на Дальнем Востоке России.

claims.statement: The nocnitsa (Polish nocnica), often plural, is a nightmare spirit or demon tormenting people, especially children, at night; East Slavic names include kriksy, plaksy, plachky.
claims.statement_id: Nocnitsa (ночница, Polandia nocnica), sering disebut dalam bentuk jamak, adalah roh atau iblis mimpi buruk yang menyiksa orang, terutama anak-anak, pada malam hari; dalam bahasa Slavia Timur juga disebut kriksy, plaksy, plachky.
claims.quote: often referred in plural, is a nightmare spirit or demon that torments people and especially children at night. Other names for notsnitsa in East Slavic languages include kriksy, plaksy, plachky

claims.statement: In Slavic mythology nochnitsy are female night spirits hostile to people; they attack children going to sleep, causing restlessness and insomnia; Slavs believed children's crying and poor sleep at night were their doing.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Slavia, nochnitsy adalah roh malam perempuan yang memusuhi manusia; mereka menyerang anak yang hendak tidur sehingga gelisah dan tak bisa tidur; bangsa Slavia percaya tangis dan tidur buruk anak di malam hari adalah ulah mereka.
claims.quote: в славянской мифологии ночные духи женского пола, враждебно настроенные по отношению к людям. Ночницы нападают на детей, готовящихся отойти ко сну, причиняя им беспокойство и вызывая бессонницу. Славяне верили, что причина детского плача, ночного крика и плохого сна является результатом деятельности ночниц.

claims.statement: In eastern Serbia nochnitsy were ugly old women in black; in Croatian belief long-haired women with clawed fingers; by scant Polish data like birds or bats.
claims.statement_id: Di Serbia timur nochnitsy digambarkan sebagai nenek buruk rupa berbaju hitam; menurut kepercayaan Kroasia perempuan berambut panjang bercakar; menurut sedikit data Polandia mirip burung atau kelelawar.
claims.quote: В восточной Сербии ночницы (сербохорв. ноћнице) представлялись в виде уродливых баб в чёрном. По хорватским поверьям ночницы (хорв. noćničine) — длинноволосые женщины с когтями на пальцах рук. По единичным польским данным, они могли быть похожими на птиц или летучих мышей.

claims.statement: In Silesia the nocnica was a female demon who choked people in their sleep, especially infants, and brought disease.
claims.statement_id: Di Silesia, nocnica adalah iblis perempuan yang mencekik orang yang tidur, terutama bayi, dan membawa penyakit.
claims.quote: Na Śląsku nocnicą nazywano demona płci żeńskiej, duszącego ludzi we śnie – zwłaszcza niemowlęta – i sprowadzającego choroby.

claims.statement: Nocnice are mentioned in, among others, Brother Rudolf's 13th-century Catalogue of Magic.
claims.statement_id: Nocnica disebut antara lain dalam Katalog Sihir Bruder Rudolf dari abad ke-13.
claims.quote: Wzmiankę o nocnicach znajdziemy m.in. w trzynastowiecznym Katalogu magii Brata Rudolfa

claims.statement: The psoglav ("doghead") is a demonic creature of Balkan mythology believed in parts of Bosnia and Montenegro, with a human body and horse legs, a dog's head with iron teeth and one eye on the forehead.
claims.statement_id: Psoglav (Псоглав, harfiah "kepala anjing") adalah makhluk mitis bersifat iblis dalam mitologi Balkan yang dipercaya di sebagian Bosnia dan Montenegro, bertubuh manusia berkaki kuda, berkepala anjing bergigi besi, dan bermata satu di dahi.
claims.quote: (Serbian Cyrillic: Псоглав , literally "doghead") is a demonic mythical creature in Balkan mythology; belief about it existed in parts of Bosnia and Montenegro. Psoglav was described as having a human body with horse legs, a dog's head with iron teeth, and a single eye on the forehead.

claims.statement: Psoglavs live in caves or a dark, gem-rich, sunless land, eat people and even dig up corpses; Croatian psoglavac, Slovene psoglavec; many legends exist, especially on the Istrian peninsula in Croatia.
claims.statement_id: Psoglav tinggal di gua atau negeri gelap yang kaya permata tanpa matahari, memakan manusia, bahkan menggali kuburan untuk memakan mayat; dalam bahasa Kroasia disebut psoglavac dan Slovenia psoglavec; banyak legenda tentangnya terutama di Semenanjung Istria, Kroasia.
claims.quote: Psoglavs were described as living in caves or in a dark land which has plenty of gemstones, but no sun. They practice anthropophagy, by eating people, or even digging out corpses from graves to eat them. In Croatian the term is psoglavac, and in Slovene it is psoglavec. There are numerous legends about them, particularly on the Istrian peninsula in Croatia.

claims.statement: This being was described as a chimera with a human body, horse legs and a dog's head, with iron teeth and one eye like the Greek cyclopes.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini digambarkan sebagai kimera bertubuh manusia, berkaki kuda, dan berkepala anjing, bergigi besi dan bermata satu seperti kiklop Yunani.
claims.quote: Ово биће је описивано као химера са људским телом, коњским ногама и псећом главом. Имало је гвоздене зубе и једно око, попут грчких киклопа.

claims.statement: Vuk Karadžić recorded psoglav in his 1818 Serbian Dictionary as "a man with a dog's head".
claims.statement_id: Vuk Karadžić dalam Kamus Serbia tahun 1818 mencatat kata psoglav dengan arti "manusia berkepala anjing".
claims.quote: Вук Караџић је у Српском рјечнику из 1818. записао реч псоглав у значењу: „човек са главом пса”.

claims.statement: The psoglav is a demon of Serbian mythology; belief in it was widespread in parts of Bosnia and Montenegro.
claims.statement_id: Psoglav adalah iblis dari mitologi Serbia; kepercayaan kepadanya tersebar di sebagian Bosnia dan Montenegro.
claims.quote: Псоглав је демон из српске митологије. Веровање у ова створења је било распрострањено у неким деловима Босне и у Црној Гори.

claims.statement: They devoured people and even dug up graves to feed on corpses.
claims.statement_id: Mereka melahap manusia dan bahkan menggali kuburan untuk memakan mayat.
claims.quote: Прождирали су људе, а чак су откопавали и гробове како би се хранили њиховим лешевима.

claims.statement: The Mistress of the Copper Mountain, also the Malachite Maid (Malakhitnitsa), is a legendary being of the Ural miners, Mistress of Russia's Ural Mountains, a figure of Slavic mythology and Russian fairy tales.
claims.statement_id: Nyonya Gunung Tembaga (Хозяйка медной горы), juga Gadis Malakit (Malakhitnitsa), adalah makhluk legendaris para penambang Ural, penguasa Pegunungan Ural di Rusia, tokoh mitologi Slavia dan dongeng Rusia.
claims.quote: is a legendary being of the Ural miners, said to be the Mistress of the Ural Mountains of Russia. A character of Slavic mythology and Russian fairy tales.

claims.statement: In lore she is an extremely beautiful green-eyed young woman in a malachite gown or a lizard; patroness of miners, protector and owner of hidden underground riches, able to permit or prevent mining in certain places.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita ia digambarkan sebagai perempuan muda sangat cantik bermata hijau bergaun malakit atau sebagai kadal; ia pelindung penambang, penjaga dan pemilik kekayaan bawah tanah, yang dapat mengizinkan atau mencegah penambangan batu dan logam di tempat tertentu.
claims.quote: In folklore or legend, she is depicted as an extremely beautiful green-eyed young woman in a malachite gown or as a lizard. She has been viewed as the patroness of miners, the protector and owner of hidden underground riches, the one who can either permit or prevent the mining of stones and metals in certain places.

claims.statement: "The Copper Mountain" is the Gumyoshevsky mine, the oldest in the Urals, now in the town of Polevskoy, Sverdlovsk Oblast.
claims.statement_id: "Gunung Tembaga" adalah tambang Gumyoshevsky, tambang tertua di Pegunungan Ural, kini di kota Polevskoy, Oblast Sverdlovsk.
claims.quote: "The Copper Mountain" is the Gumyoshevsky mine, the oldest mine of the Ural Mountains, which was called "The Copper Mountain" or simply "The Mountain" by the populace. It is now located in the town of Polevskoy, Sverdlovsk Oblast.

claims.statement: She can appear as a lizard, sometimes crowned, and commands the mountain lizards; she may also become a snake.
claims.statement_id: Ia dapat tampil sebagai kadal, kadang bermahkota, dan memerintah kadal-kadal gunung; ia juga dapat menjelma ular.
claims.quote: The mistress can appear as a lizard herself, sometimes wearing a crown, and has the mountain lizards under her command. She may also assume the form of a snake

claims.statement: By legend whoever sees the Mistress falls under her spell; she is kind to good people and skilled craftsmen, helping them find jewels and gold, but if her conditions are not met the person loses all luck and skill and may even die.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, orang yang melihatnya jatuh di bawah pengaruhnya; ia baik kepada orang baik dan pengrajin terampil, membantu mereka menemukan permata dan emas, tetapi bila syaratnya tak dipenuhi orang itu kehilangan keberuntungan dan keterampilan, bahkan bisa mati.
claims.quote: According to legend, a person who sees the Mistress comes under her spell. She shows kindness to good people and skilled craftsmen, helping them to find jewels and gold, but if her conditions aren't met, the person loses all his luck and skill, and can even die.

claims.statement: The Mistress became well known through Pavel Bazhov's collection of Ural folktales, The Malachite Box.
claims.statement_id: Nyonya Gunung Tembaga menjadi tokoh terkenal lewat kumpulan cerita rakyat Ural karya Pavel Bazhov, Kotak Malakit (The Malachite Box).
claims.quote: The Mistress of the Copper Mountain became a well known character from her appearance in Pavel Bazhov's collection of Ural Mountains folktales (also known as skaz) under the title The Malachite Box.

claims.statement: The coat of arms of Polevskoy shows the Mistress of the Copper Mountain as a golden lizard.
claims.statement_id: Lambang kota Polevskoy menampilkan Nyonya Gunung Tembaga sebagai kadal emas.
claims.quote: The coat of arms of Polevskoy (from left to right): the Venus symbol (♀), which represents the chemical element copper and was the brand of the Polevskoy Copper Smelting Plant, the Mistress of the Copper Mountain depicted as the golden lizard

claims.statement: The vourdalak is a kind of vampire originating in Russian literature; some Western sources call it a "Russian vampire" that must drink the blood of its loved ones and convert its whole family.
claims.statement_id: Vourdalak adalah sejenis vampir yang berasal dari sastra Rusia; sebagian sumber Barat menyebutnya "vampir Rusia" yang harus meminum darah orang-orang yang dicintainya dan mengubah seluruh keluarganya.
claims.quote: is a kind of vampire originating in Russian literature. Some Western sources define it as a type of "Russian vampire" that must consume the blood of its loved ones and convert its whole family.

claims.statement: This notion apparently rests on Alexey K. Tolstoy's novella The Family of the Vourdalak, about one such Slavic family.
claims.statement_id: Gagasan ini tampaknya bersumber dari novela Alexey K. Tolstoy, Keluarga Vourdalak, yang mengisahkan satu keluarga Slavia semacam itu.
claims.quote: This notion is based apparently on Alexey K. Tolstoy's novella The Family of the Vourdalak, telling the story of one such Slavic family.

claims.statement: Today the upyr and vourdalak are regarded as synonymous, but in the 19th century they were seen as separate but similar beings.
claims.statement_id: Kini upyr dan vourdalak dianggap sinonim, tetapi pada abad ke-19 keduanya dipandang makhluk yang berbeda walau mirip.
claims.quote: Nowadays, the upyr and vourdalak are regarded as synonymous; however, in the 19th century, they were seen as separate but similar entities.

claims.statement: In Russian the word vourdalak first appeared in the early 19th century and became common through Alexander Pushkin's 1836 poem of that name, part of the Songs of the Western Slavs cycle.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Rusia kata vourdalak (вурдалак) pertama muncul pada awal abad ke-19 dan menjadi umum berkat puisi Alexander Pushkin tahun 1836 berjudul sama, bagian dari siklus Lagu-lagu Slavia Barat (Songs of the Western Slavs).
claims.quote: In the Russian language, the word vourdalak first appeared in the early 19th century, and became common due to Alexander Pushkin's 1836 poem of the same name, part of the Songs of the Western Slavs cycle.

claims.statement: It is a corrupt form of the West Slavic volkodlak, literally "wolf-fur" or "wolf-hide", someone "wearing" a wolf's skin, a werewolf.
claims.statement_id: Kata itu bentuk rusak dari kata Slavia Barat volkodlak, harfiah "bulu serigala" atau "kulit serigala", yaitu orang yang "memakai" kulit serigala, manusia serigala.
claims.quote: It is the corrupt form of the West Slavic word volkodlak ... meaning literally 'wolf-fur' or 'wolf-hide', denoting someone "wearing" a wolf's skin, a werewolf.

claims.statement: This vampire tends to attack members of its own family first, drinking their blood and turning them into vourdalaks in turn.
claims.statement_id: Vampir ini cenderung menyerang anggota keluarganya lebih dulu, meminum darah mereka dan mengubah mereka menjadi vourdalak pula.
claims.quote: Ce vampire se caractérise par sa propension à s'attaquer prioritairement aux membres de sa famille en buvant leur sang et les transformant en vourdalaks à leur tour.

claims.statement: The wurdulac also appears in the horror film Black Sabbath, segment "The Wurdulak", an adaptation of Tolstoy's The Family of the Vourdalak.
claims.statement_id: Wurdulac juga muncul dalam film horor Black Sabbath, segmen "The Wurdulak", adaptasi Keluarga Vourdalak karya Tolstoy.
claims.quote: The wurdulac also appears in the horror film Black Sabbath: "The Wurdulak", which is an adaptation of Tolstoy's The Family of the Vourdalak.

claims.statement: Other sources suggest Pushkin borrowed and adapted the word from Lord Byron's "The Giaour", whose footnote claims the Greek word for vampire is "Vardoulacha".
claims.statement_id: Sumber lain menduga Pushkin memungut dan menyesuaikan kata itu dari puisi Lord Byron, "The Giaour", yang memuat catatan kaki bahwa kata Yunani untuk vampir adalah "Vardoulacha".
claims.quote: Other sources suggest that Pushkin borrowed and adapted the word from Lord Byron's "The Giaour", which contains a footnote claiming that the Greek word for a vampire is "Vardoulacha".

claims.statement: The Russian upyr was said to be a former witch, werewolf or particularly nasty sinner excommunicated from the church.
claims.statement_id: Upyr Rusia konon dulunya penyihir, manusia serigala, atau pendosa yang sangat jahat yang telah dikucilkan dari gereja.
claims.quote: The Russian upyr was said to be a former witch, werewolf or a particularly nasty sinner who had been excommunicated from the church.

claims.statement: "The Vourdalak" is the second part of Mario Bava's 1963 film (Black Sabbath), based on Alexey Tolstoy's novella The Family of the Vourdalak.
claims.statement_id: "Vourdalak" (Вурдалак) adalah bagian kedua film Mario Bava tahun 1963 (Три лика страха, Black Sabbath), berdasarkan novela Alexey Tolstoy, Keluarga Vourdalak.
claims.quote: «Вурдалак» — вторая часть фильма Марио Бавы «Три лика страха» (1963), поставленная по повести Алексея Толстого «Семья вурдалака».

claims.statement: The 2023 French horror-drama film The Vourdalak also centres on them.
claims.statement_id: Film horor-drama Prancis tahun 2023, The Vourdalak, juga berpusat pada makhluk ini.
claims.quote: The 2023 French horror-drama film The Vourdalak also centres on them.

claims.statement: "The Vourdalak" is a poem by Alexander Pushkin from the Songs of the Western Slavs cycle (1834).
claims.statement_id: "Vourdalak" (Вурдалак) adalah puisi Alexander Pushkin dari siklus Lagu-lagu Slavia Barat (Песни западных славян) tahun 1834.
claims.quote: «Вурдалак» — стихотворение Александра Пушкина из цикла «Песни западных славян» (1834).

claims.statement: Azhdahak is the Armenian form of the Avestan demon Azhi Dahaka's name; in Iranian myth he is imprisoned in Mount Damavand but will break out at the end of time, finally to be defeated by Fereydun.
claims.statement_id: Azhdahak adalah bentuk Armenia dari nama iblis Avesta Azhi Dahaka; dalam mitologi Iran ia dipenjara di Gunung Damavand, tetapi pada akhir zaman akan lepas dan akhirnya dikalahkan Fereydun.
claims.quote: is the Armenian form of the name of the Avestan demon Azhi Dahaka. In Iranian mythology, he is imprisoned in Mount Damavand, but will at the end of time break out, to be ultimately defeated by Fereydun.

claims.statement: In his History of Armenia, the Armenian writer Movses Khorenatsi identified Azhdahak with the Median king Astyages.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Sejarah Armenia (History of Armenia), penulis Armenia Movses Khorenatsi menyamakan Azhdahak dengan raja Media, Astyages.
claims.quote: In his History of Armenia, the Armenian writer Movses Khorenatsi identified Azhdahak with the Median king Astyages

claims.statement: The Armenian form Azhdahak was borrowed from Parthian.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk Armenia Azhdahak dipinjam dari bahasa Parthia.
claims.quote: The Armenian form Azhdahak was borrowed from Parthian

claims.statement: Ajdahak is a dragon-king of Armenian mythology; the vishaps, the class of dragons he belongs to, live in high mountains, great lakes, the sky and clouds.
claims.statement_id: Ajdahak adalah raja-naga dalam mitologi Armenia; para vishap (vichaps), golongan naga tempat Ajdahak berada, hidup di gunung tinggi, danau besar, langit, dan awan.
claims.quote: est un roi-dragon, personnage de la mythologie arménienne. Les vichaps, la catégorie de dragons à laquelle appartient Ajdahak, vivent dans les hautes montagnes, les grands lacs, le ciel et les nuages.

claims.statement: When they rise to the sky or come down from it, especially towards lakes, their roar terrifies the people.
claims.statement_id: Ketika naik ke langit atau turun darinya, terutama menuju danau, raungan mereka menakutkan penduduk.
claims.quote: Lorsqu'ils montent vers le ciel ou qu'ils en descendent, notamment en direction de lacs, leur rugissement provoque l'effroi des populations.

claims.statement: According to Movses Khorenatsi, he was said to have been killed by a king named Tigran.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Movses Khorenatsi, ia konon dibunuh oleh raja bernama Tigran (Tigrane).
claims.quote: Il aurait été tué par un roi nommé Tigrane.

claims.statement: The movement of azhdahaks underground causes earthquakes; a vishap that lives to a thousand years can swallow the whole world.
claims.statement_id: Gerakan para azhdahak di bawah tanah menyebabkan gempa bumi; vishap yang hidup sampai seribu tahun dapat menelan seluruh dunia.
claims.quote: Движение аждааков под землёй вызывает землетрясения. Доживший до тысячи лет вишап может поглотить весь мир.

claims.statement: In the ancient Armenian epic Vipasank, Azhdahak was king of the Mars (Medes), defeated by the Armenian king Tigran I Yervanduni.
claims.statement_id: Dalam epos Armenia kuno Vipasank (Випасанк), Azhdahak adalah raja bangsa Mar (Media) yang dikalahkan raja Armenia Tigran I (Тигран I Ервандид).
claims.quote: В древнеармянском эпосе «Випасанк» Аждаак был царём маров (мидийцев), которого побеждает армянский царь Тигран I Ервандид.

claims.statement: Azhdahak, from Avestan Aži Dahāka, "serpent king", is a man-vishap (man-dragon) in Armenian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Nama Azhdahak (Աժդահակ) berasal dari Avesta Aži Dahāka, "raja ular"; ia manusia-vishap (manusia-naga) dalam mitologi Armenia.
claims.quote: от авест. Aži Dahāka «змеиный царь») — человек-вишап (человек-дракон) в армянской мифологии.

claims.statement: In Old Armenian the name is Աժդահակ, also spelled Ashdahak.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Armenia Kuno namanya Աժդահակ, juga dieja Ashdahak.
claims.quote: (Old Armenian: Աժդահակ , also spelled Ashdahak)

claims.statement: Bangpūtys is a male deity of Lithuanian mythology; from very scanty sources some mythologists have reconstructed him as a god of sea and storm.
claims.statement_id: Bangpūtys adalah nama dewa laki-laki dalam mitologi Lituania; berdasarkan sumber yang sangat sedikit, sebagian ahli mitologi merekonstruksinya sebagai dewa laut dan badai.
claims.quote: Bangpūtys is the name of a masculine deity in Lithuanian mythology. Basing on very scanty sources, some mythologists have reconstructed him as a god of sea and storm.

claims.statement: According to the reconstructions he is austere and unrelenting, bearded, winged and two-faced, commonly shown with a fish in his left hand, a utensil in his right and a rooster on his head.
claims.statement_id: Menurut rekonstruksi, ia keras dan tak kenal ampun, berjanggut, bersayap, dan bermuka dua, biasanya digambarkan memegang ikan di tangan kiri, perkakas di tangan kanan, dan ayam jantan di kepala.
claims.quote: According to the reconstructions, he is austere and unrelenting. He has a beard, wings and two faces. He is commonly portrayed as having a fish in his left hand, a utensil in his right hand, and a rooster on the head.

claims.statement: His sons are the wind gods Rytys, Pietys, Šiaurys and Vakaris (east, south, north and west).
claims.statement_id: Anak-anaknya adalah dewa-dewa angin: Rytys, Pietys, Šiaurys, dan Vakaris (angin timur, selatan, utara, dan barat).
claims.quote: His sons are the gods of wind: Rytys, Pietys, Šiaurys and Vakaris (easterly, southern, northern and westerly).

claims.statement: Bangpūtys is thought very vindictive; one story tells how Auštaras (son of Aušrinė and Mėnuo, the other east wind god) swam in the sea and made a storm, and Bangpūtys wanted to drown him.
claims.statement_id: Bangpūtys dianggap dewa yang sangat pendendam; satu kisah menceritakan Auštaras (anak Aušrinė dan Mėnuo, dewa angin timur lainnya) berenang di laut dan membuat badai, lalu Bangpūtys ingin menenggelamkannya.
claims.quote: Bangpūtys is considered a very vindictive god, for example, one story talks of how Auštaras (son of Aušrinė and Mėnuo, the other god of easterly wind) was swimming in the sea and made a storm. Bangpūtys wanted to drown him.

claims.statement: Bangpūtys is the Lithuanian and Prussian god of sea storms, wind and waves.
claims.statement_id: Bangpūtys (Бангпутис) adalah dewa Lituania dan Prusia untuk badai laut, angin, dan ombak.
claims.quote: литовский и прусский бог морских бурь, штормов, ветра и волн.

claims.statement: His name means "he who blows on the waves"; in the 18th century he was considered a sea god and compared to Neptune.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berarti "yang meniup ombak"; pada abad ke-18 (XVIII) ia dianggap dewa laut dan dibandingkan dengan Neptunus.
claims.quote: Имя означает «Веющий на волны». В XVIII веке считался богом моря и сравнивался с Нептуном.

claims.statement: He was most often shown as a great-winged angel; to keep storms off the sea, people usually offered him straw.
claims.statement_id: Ia paling sering digambarkan sebagai malaikat bersayap besar; agar laut tidak berbadai, orang biasanya mempersembahkan jerami kepadanya.
claims.quote: Чаще всего изображался в виде большекрылого ангела. Чтобы на море не было штормов, ему обычно приносили в жертву солому.

claims.statement: The German ethnographer Matejs Pretorejs in the late 17th century called Bangpūtys a god of storm and water who received offerings, contrasting him with fire.
claims.statement_id: Etnograf Jerman Matejs Pretorejs pada akhir abad ke-17 menyebut Bangpūtys (Bangpyuts) dewa badai dan air yang diberi persembahan, dan mempertentangkannya dengan api.
claims.quote: Vuocu etnografs Matejs Pretorejs 17 godu symteņa beiguos Bangpyuti nūsauce por vātrys i iudiņa dīvu, kam asūt bejs upurāts, pretnūstatūt tū uguņam.

claims.statement: He is sometimes called by another name, Vėjadievis, and may be identical with Vėjopatis.
claims.statement_id: Ia kadang disebut dengan nama lain Vėjadievis (Веядевис), dan mungkin identik dengan Vėjopatis (Вейопатис).
claims.quote: Иногда называется другим именем Веядевис (лит. Vėjadievis). Возможно, идентичен Вейопатису.

claims.statement: In Old Prussian his name is Bangputtis; he is an ancient sea god of western Lithuanian and Prussian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Prusia Kuno namanya Bangputtis; ia dewa laut kuno dalam mitologi Lituania barat dan Prusia.
claims.quote: 고대 프로이센어: Bangputtis )는 서부 리투아니아 신화와 프로이센 신화의 고대 바다의 신이다.

claims.statement: Božić in Slavic paganism is a being symbolising the New Year, spring and youth, appearing in Christmas customs with a golden-horned deer and a pig, as opposed to Badnjak.
claims.statement_id: Božić dalam paganisme Slavia adalah makhluk yang melambangkan tahun baru, musim semi, dan masa muda, yang muncul dalam adat Natal bersama rusa bertanduk emas dan babi, sebagai lawan Badnjak.
claims.quote: in Slavic paganism is a creature symbolizing the New Year, spring and youth. It appears in Christmas customs accompanied by a golden-horned deer and a pig, as opposed to Badnjak.

claims.statement: In South Slavic languages the word passed into the modern name for Christmas, e.g. Serbian Божић, Croatian Božić and Slovenian Božič.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa-bahasa Slavia Selatan kata ini beralih menjadi nama Natal modern, misalnya Божић dalam bahasa Serbia, Božić dalam bahasa Kroasia, dan Božič dalam bahasa Slovenia.
claims.quote: In the languages of the South Slavs, the word was transferred to the modern name of Christmas, e.g. Serbian Божић, Croatian Božić and Slovenian Božič.

claims.statement: The figure of Božić is probably an echo of the cult of Svarog; Božić is the personification of the sun, which allegedly dies and is born every year.
claims.statement_id: Sosok Božić mungkin gema pemujaan Svarog; Božić adalah perwujudan matahari yang konon mati dan lahir setiap tahun.
claims.quote: The figure of Bozić is probably an echo of the cult of Svarog. Bozić is the personification of the sun, which allegedly dies and is born every year

claims.statement: He is mentioned in the koliadki (ritual songs), and his symbol is a golden-antlered deer; he marks the start of the new solar cycle at the winter solstice.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut dalam koliadki (nyanyian ritual), dan lambangnya rusa bertanduk emas; ia menandai awal siklus matahari yang baru pada titik balik musim dingin.
claims.quote: Il est mentionné dans les koliadki (chants rituels). Son symbole est un cerf aux bois d'or

claims.statement: Badnjak (the past year) burns in the fire while Božić (the new year) brings the renewal of the sun, the rebirth of spring and the rejuvenation of nature.
claims.statement_id: Badnjak (Badniak, tahun yang lalu) terbakar dalam api, sedangkan Božić (tahun baru) membawa pembaruan matahari, kelahiran kembali musim semi, dan peremajaan alam.
claims.quote: Badniak (l'année passée) brûle dans le feu alors que Bojitch (nouvel an) apporte le renouveau du soleil, la renaissance du printemps, le rajeunissement de la nature

claims.statement: In contrast to Badnjak (the old year), Božić is considered a young god, usually Badnjak's son, linked with youth, Christmas and the new year.
claims.statement_id: Berlawanan dengan Badnjak (Бадняк, tahun yang lama), Božić (Божич) dianggap dewa muda, biasanya putra Badnjak, yang dikaitkan dengan masa muda, Natal, dan tahun baru.
claims.quote: В противоположность Бадняку (старому году), Божич считается молодым богом (как правило, сыном Бадняка) и соотносится с молодостью, Рождеством и новым годом.

claims.statement: Semantically, the name Božić is a patronymic meaning "son of god".
claims.statement_id: Dari segi makna, nama Božić (Божич) adalah patronim yang berarti "putra dewa".
claims.quote: Происхождение имени Божич из семантики — это патроним (отчество), обозначающий «сына бога»

claims.statement: The figure of Božić is probably an echo of the cult of Svarozhich (Swarożyc).
claims.statement_id: Sosok Božić (Bożicz) mungkin gema pemujaan Svarozhich (Swarożyc).
claims.quote: Postać Bożicza jest prawdopodobnie echem kultu Swarożyca.

claims.statement: The cikavac is a mythical creature of Serbian mythology, imagined as a winged animal (a bird) with a long beak and a pelican-like pouch.
claims.statement_id: Cikavac adalah makhluk mitos dalam mitologi Serbia, dibayangkan sebagai hewan bersayap (burung) berparuh panjang dengan kantong seperti pelikan.
claims.quote: is a mythical creature in Serbian mythology, imagined as a winged animal (a bird) with long beak and a pelican-like sack.

claims.statement: A cikavac could be acquired from a black hen's egg carried by a woman under her armpit for 40 days, during which she would not confess, cut nails, wash her face or pray.
claims.statement_id: Cikavac dapat diperoleh dengan mengambil telur ayam betina hitam, yang lalu dibawa seorang perempuan di bawah ketiak selama 40 hari, tanpa mengaku dosa, memotong kuku, membasuh muka, atau berdoa.
claims.quote: A cikavac could be acquired by taking an egg from a black hen, which would then be carried by a woman under her armpit for 40 days, during which time one would not confess, cut nails, wash face or pray.

claims.statement: The cikavac would then suck honey from others' beehives and milk from others' cattle and bring it to its owner; it fulfilled any wish and let the owner understand animal language.
claims.statement_id: Cikavac lalu mengisap madu dari sarang lebah orang lain dan susu ternak orang lain lalu membawanya kepada pemiliknya; ia memenuhi setiap keinginan pemilik dan membuatnya mengerti bahasa hewan.
claims.quote: The cikavac would then suck honey from others' beehives and milk of others' cattle, and bring it to the owner; it would fulfill any owner's wish, and also enable its owner to understand the animal language.

claims.statement: In the Czech Republic the plivník is a sprite that fills the same role as the cikavac.
claims.statement_id: Di Republik Ceko, plivník adalah makhluk kecil (lutin) yang memainkan peran sama seperti cikavac.
claims.quote: En République tchèque, le plivník est un lutin qui remplit le même rôle que le cikavac.

claims.statement: The cikavac is a legendary creature of Serbian mythology with long wings and a throat pouch.
claims.statement_id: Cikavac adalah makhluk legendaris mitologi Serbia bersayap panjang dengan kantong tenggorokan.
claims.quote: est une créature légendaire de la mythologie serbe doté de longues ailes et d'un sac gulaire.

claims.statement: A cikavac would suck honey and milk from others' hives and livestock to bring to its master, fulfil his every wish, and make him able to understand the language of animals.
claims.statement_id: Cikavac akan mengisap madu dan susu dari sarang lebah dan ternak orang lain untuk dibawa kepada tuannya, memenuhi setiap keinginannya, dan membuatnya mampu memahami bahasa hewan.
claims.quote: Un cikavac avrebbe poi succhiato il miele e il latte dagli alveari e dal bestiame altrui per portarlo al suo padrone, avrebbe soddisfatto ogni suo desiderio e l'avrebbe anche reso in grado di comprendere il linguaggio degli animali.

claims.statement: Devil Boruta is a figure of Polish mythology, folklore and literature associated with the Polish town of Łęczyca.
claims.statement_id: Iblis Boruta (Diabeł Boruta) adalah tokoh dari mitologi, cerita rakyat, dan sastra Polandia yang dikaitkan dengan kota Łęczyca di Polandia.
claims.quote: is a fictional character from Polish mythology, folklore and literature, who is associated with the Polish town of Łęczyca.

claims.statement: The figure is a post-Christianisation transformation of the pagan Slavic leshy; Boruta is also called błotnik, a swamp spirit.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh ini perubahan wujud leshy pagan Slavia pada masa setelah Kristenisasi; Boruta juga disebut błotnik, roh rawa.
claims.quote: The character is the transformation of the pagan Slavic leshy in post-Christianization times. Boruta is also referred to as błotnik, a swamp spirit.

claims.statement: Devil Boruta, also called błotnik, is a fictional figure, a devil dwelling in the vaults of the castle in Łęczyca.
claims.statement_id: Iblis Boruta, juga disebut błotnik, adalah tokoh rekaan, iblis yang tinggal di ruang bawah tanah kastel di Łęczyca.
claims.quote: Diabeł Boruta, zwany też błotnikiem – fikcyjna postać, diabeł zamieszkujący podziemia zamku w Łęczycy.

claims.statement: He was usually considered a nobleman, busy corrupting nobles and leaving other classes to other devils, like Rokita of the same region, who more often tempted peasants.
claims.statement_id: Ia biasanya dianggap bangsawan dan sibuk merusak para bangsawan, menyerahkan golongan lain kepada iblis lain, seperti Rokita dari daerah yang sama yang lebih sering menggoda petani.
claims.quote: He was usually considered to be a nobleman, and accordingly, he was usually busy with corrupting nobles, leaving other social classes to other devils - like Rokita the devil from the same region, who more often tempted peasants.

claims.statement: He was a tall nobleman with long black moustaches and black eyes, wearing a rich kontusz that hid his tail and a cap that hid his horns.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai szlachcic (bangsawan) tinggi dengan kumis hitam panjang dan mata hitam, mengenakan kontusz mewah yang menutupi ekor dan topi yang menutupi tanduk; ia juga muncul sebagai penggiling (młynarz) yang mendatangi kincir pada malam hari.
claims.quote: Był to wysoki szlachcic z długimi, czarnymi wąsiskami, o czarnych oczach, ubrany w bogaty kontusz zakrywający ogon i czapkę zasłaniającą rogi.

claims.statement: He was also met as a bird with huge wings (Boruta błotny) in the meadows and marshes near Łęczyca.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga terlihat sebagai burung bersayap besar (Boruta błotny) di padang dan rawa sekitar Łęczyca, juga sebagai ikan bertanduk, kuda hitam, burung hantu (sowa), dan serigala (wilk).
claims.quote: jako ptak z ogromnymi skrzydłami (Boruta błotny – Błotnik) spotykany był na podłęczyckich łąkach i moczarach,

claims.statement: His presence could be shown by a fire that suddenly flares and quickly dies; in all legends Boruta shows great cunning, wit and superhuman strength.
claims.statement_id: Kehadiran iblis ini dapat ditandai api yang tiba-tiba menyala lalu cepat padam; dalam semua legenda Boruta menunjukkan kelicikan, kecerdikan, dan kekuatan melebihi manusia, walau dalam banyak legenda ia juga dermawan bagi orang miskin.
claims.quote: Obecność tego diabła mógł też potwierdzać nagle zapalający się i szybko gasnący ogień. We wszystkich legendach poświęconych diabłu Borucie wykazuje się on dużą przebiegłością, sprytem oraz nadludzką siłą.

claims.statement: Zygmunt Gloger and some other ethnologists held that dressing Boruta as a nobleman is 19th-century fakelore reintroduced into folklore.
claims.statement_id: Zygmunt Gloger dan sejumlah etnolog lain menganggap gambaran Boruta berpakaian bangsawan sebagai folklor palsu abad ke-19 yang dimasukkan kembali ke cerita rakyat.
claims.quote: Zygmunt Gloger and some other ethnologists believed that dressing Boruta as a nobleman is fakelore produced in the 19th century and reintroduced into folklore.

claims.statement: Stories of Boruta scaring people at night on dams and in forests, leading them astray and sometimes appearing as a black dog, circulated throughout the country.
claims.statement_id: Kisah tentang Boruta, yang sibuk menakuti orang pada malam hari di bendungan dan hutan, menyesatkan mereka, dan kadang muncul sebagai anjing hitam, beredar di seluruh negeri.
claims.quote: Stories about Boruta, who was busy scaring people at night on dams and in forests and playing mischief by leading them astray, and who sometimes appeared in the form of a black dog, circulated throughout the country

claims.statement: Linde defined the word as "the devil borowiec (forest spirit), błotnik (swamp spirit), an evil spirit living, by peasant tales, in swamps and muddy places".
claims.statement_id: Linde mendefinisikan kata ini sebagai "iblis borowiec (roh hutan), błotnik (roh rawa), roh jahat yang menurut dongeng petani tinggal di rawa dan tempat berlumpur".
claims.quote: "The devil borowiec [forest spirit], błotnik [swamp spirit], an evil spirit, according to peasant fairy tales, living in swamps and muddy places."

claims.statement: The Skarbnik ("treasurer"), or Kladenets, is a spirit living in mines and underground workings, guardian of gems, crystals and precious metals.
claims.statement_id: Skarbnik (dari bahasa Polandia skarbnik, "bendahara"), atau Kladenets (Скарбник, Кладенец), adalah roh yang tinggal di tambang dan lorong bawah tanah, penjaga permata, kristal, dan logam mulia.
claims.quote: is a spirit who lives in mines and underground workings and is the guardian of gems, crystals, and precious metals.

claims.statement: He is said to protect miners from danger, lead them back when lost, and lead them to veins of ore.
claims.statement_id: Konon ia melindungi penambang dari bahaya, menuntun mereka kembali bila tersesat, dan menunjukkan urat bijih.
claims.quote: It is said that he will protect miners from danger and lead them back when they are lost. He will also lead them to veins of ore.

claims.statement: To those who are evil or insult him he is deadly, pushing them into dark chasms or bringing tunnels down on them.
claims.statement_id: Terhadap orang jahat atau yang menghinanya ia mematikan: mendorong mereka ke jurang gelap atau meruntuhkan terowongan menimpa mereka.
claims.quote: To people who are evil or insult him, he is deadly, pushing them into dark chasms or send tunnels crashing down upon them.

claims.statement: Throwing rocks, whistling or covering one's head offend the Skarbnik, who warns the offender with handfuls of soil before acting seriously.
claims.statement_id: Melempar batu, bersiul, atau menutup kepala menyinggung Skarbnik, yang akan memperingatkan pelaku dengan melemparkan segenggam tanah sebelum bertindak lebih keras.
claims.quote: Hurling rocks, whistling, or covering one's head are actions that are offensive to Skarbnik, who will warn the offender with handfuls of pelted soil in their direction before taking serious action.

claims.statement: Karzełek (diminutive of karzeł, a small person or non-fantastic dwarf) or Skarbnik ("the Treasurer") in Polish mythology lives in mines and underground workings.
claims.statement_id: Karzełek (diminutif dari karzeł, orang kecil atau kerdil non-fantastis) atau Skarbnik ("Bendahara") dalam mitologi Polandia tinggal di tambang dan lorong bawah tanah.
claims.quote: O Karzełek (diminutivo de karzeł – um pequeno, usado para descrever um anão não-fantástico) ou Skarbnik (o Tesoureiro) na mitologia polonesa vive em minas e no funcionamento do subterrâneo.

claims.statement: In Slavic belief the Skarbnik is a spirit of the underground, especially mines, guarding the earth's resources and buried treasure, and ruler of an underground realm to which he took the souls of miners killed at work.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan Slavia, Skarbnik (дзедка dalam bahasa Belarus, Dzedka) adalah roh penghuni alam bawah tanah, terutama tambang, penjaga kekayaan alam bumi dan harta terkubur, sekaligus penguasa alam bawah tanah tempat ia membawa jiwa penambang yang tewas di tambang.
claims.quote: w wierzeniach słowiańskich duch zamieszkujący podziemia (zwłaszcza kopalnie), strzegący naturalnych zasobów ziemi i zakopanych w niej skarbów. Był także władcą podziemnej krainy, do której zabierał dusze górników, którzy zginęli podczas pracy w kopalni.

claims.statement: He mostly appeared as an old bearded miner with a lamp, could take the shape of a goat, horse, dog, mouse, frog, spider or fly, and could stay invisible, when a miner might sense him or hear knocking.
claims.statement_id: Ia paling sering tampil sebagai penambang tua berjanggut membawa pelita, dapat menjelma kambing, kuda, anjing, tikus, katak, laba-laba, atau lalat, dan dapat tetap tak terlihat sehingga penambang hanya merasakan kehadirannya atau mendengar ketukan; ia juga memperingatkan penambang akan runtuhan, banjir, dan kebakaran.
claims.quote: Ukazywał się najczęściej pod postacią starego, brodatego górnika z kagankiem w ręku, potrafił też przybrać kształt kozy, konia, psa, myszy, żaby, pająka, muchy. Mógł także pozostawać niewidzialny, wówczas górnik mógł wyczuć jego obecność bądź słyszeć stukanie.

claims.statement: In Romanian folklore Muma Pădurii is an ugly, mischievous or mad old woman living in the forest (deep virgin forest, a hut or an old tree), the opposite of fairies such as the Zână, and protector of animals and plants who brews potions and helps injured animals.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Rumania, Muma Pădurii adalah perempuan tua buruk rupa yang nakal atau gila, tinggal di hutan (jantung hutan perawan, pondok, atau pohon tua), lawan peri seperti Zână, sekaligus pelindung hewan dan tumbuhan yang meracik ramuan dan menolong hewan terluka.
claims.quote: is an ugly and mischievous or mad old woman living in the forest (in the heart of virgin forests, in a hut/cabin, or an old tree). She is the opposite of fairies such as Zână. She is also the protector of the animals and plants, brewing potions and helping injured animals.

claims.statement: She cures a dying forest and keeps trespassers away by driving them mad and scaring them.
claims.statement_id: Ia menyembuhkan hutan yang sekarat dan mengusir penyusup dengan membuat mereka gila dan ketakutan; ia makhluk netral yang hanya mencelakai orang yang merusak hutan.
claims.quote: She cures the forest if it is dying and she keeps unwanted trespassers away by driving them mad and scaring them.

claims.statement: Muma Pădurii literally means "mother of the forest"; "mumă" is an archaic form of "mamă" (mother) with a fairy-tale overtone for Romanian readers.
claims.statement_id: Muma Pădurii harfiah berarti "ibu hutan"; "mumă" adalah bentuk kuno dari "mamă" (ibu) yang bernuansa dongeng bagi pembaca Rumania.
claims.quote: Muma Pădurii literally means "mother of the forest", though "mumă" is an archaic version of "mamă" (mother), which has a fairy tale overtone for the Romanian reader

claims.statement: Muma Pădurii is a forest spirit in the body of a very ugly old woman; she can sometimes change shape and usually lives in a dark, dreadful, hidden little house.
claims.statement_id: Muma Pădurii adalah roh hutan dalam tubuh perempuan yang sangat buruk rupa dan tua; kadang ia dapat berubah wujud, dan biasanya tinggal di rumah kecil yang gelap, mengerikan, dan tersembunyi.
claims.quote: Mumă Pădurii es un espíritu del bosque en el cuerpo de una mujer muy fea y anciana. A veces tiene la habilidad de cambiar de forma. Suele vivir en una casita oscura, terrible y escondida.

claims.statement: She is believed to attack children, so a great variety of spells (descântece in Romanian) are used against her.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipercaya menyerang anak-anak, sehingga banyak mantra (descântece dalam bahasa Rumania) dipakai untuk melawannya.
claims.quote: Se cree que ataca a los niños y debido a esto se utilizan una gran variedad de hechizos (descântece en rumano) contra ella.

claims.statement: In one popular tale she tries to boil a little girl alive in a cauldron, but the girl's brother outwits Muma Pădurii and pushes her into the oven, as in Hansel and Gretel.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu kisah populer ia hendak merebus seorang gadis kecil hidup-hidup dalam kuali, tetapi kakak gadis itu mengakali Muma Pădurii dan mendorongnya ke dalam tungku, seperti kisah Hansel dan Gretel (Hansel y Gretel).
claims.quote: En una de las historias populares, intenta hervir viva a una niña en un caldero. Sin embargo, el hermano de la niña es más astuto que Mumă Pădurii y empuja a la mujer-monstruo al horno, como en el cuento de Hansel y Gretel.

claims.statement: Instead of "she's ugly", Romanians sometimes say "she looks like Muma Pădurii".
claims.statement_id: Alih-alih berkata "ia jelek", orang Rumania kadang berkata "ia mirip Muma Pădurii".
claims.quote: Instead of saying "She's ugly", Romanians sometimes say "She looks like Muma Pădurii".

claims.statement: Muma Pădurii can be compared with witches of other folklores, such as the wicked witch of the Grimms' Hansel and Gretel in Germany, or Baba Yaga of Russian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Muma Pădurii dapat dibandingkan dengan penyihir dari cerita rakyat lain, seperti penyihir jahat dalam kisah Hansel dan Gretel (João e Maria) dari Grimm di Jerman (Alemanha), atau Baba Yaga dari cerita rakyat Rusia.
claims.quote: Muma Pădurii pode ser comparada à outras bruxas de folclores diferentes como a bruxa má de João e Maria dos contos dos irmãos Grimm na Alemanha (antiga Prússia), ou à Baba Yaga do folclore russo

claims.statement: Muma Pădurii ("Mother of the Forest") is also known as Pădureanca or Muma Huciului.
claims.statement_id: Muma Pădurii ("Ibu Hutan") juga dikenal sebagai Pădureanca atau Muma Huciului.
claims.quote: Muma Pădurii (em tradução livre "Mãe da Floresta" em romeno, também conhecida como Pădureanca ou Muma Huciului)

claims.statement: Ochokochi ("goat-man") is a figure of Georgian mythology, especially the Colchian and Mingrelian groups; instead of hair on his breast he has a pointed bone or stone-axe protrusion, and he attacks passers-by, killing them by embracing them.
claims.statement_id: Ochokochi (ოჩოკოჩი, harfiah "manusia-kambing") adalah tokoh mitologi Georgia, terutama kelompok Kolkhis (Colchian) dan Mingrelia; alih-alih bulu di dada ia memiliki tonjolan berbentuk tulang runcing atau kapak batu, dan ia menyerang orang yang lewat lalu membunuh mereka dengan memeluknya.
claims.quote: is a figure from Georgian mythology, particularly the Colchian and Mingrelian ethnic groups. Instead of hair on his breast, he has a protuberance in the form of a pointed bone or a stone-axe. He attacks passers by, whom he kills by embracing them.

claims.statement: In Georgian mythology Ochokochi is a half-man, half-goat evil forest deity in constant conflict with hunters and gatherers.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Georgia, Ochokochi (Очокочи) adalah makhluk setengah manusia setengah kambing, dewa hutan jahat yang selalu berkonflik dengan pemburu dan pengumpul.
claims.quote: в грузинской мифологии получеловек-полукозёл, злое лесное божество, находящееся в постоянном конфликте с охотниками и собирателями.

claims.statement: By legend Ochokochi was a huge monster covered in rust-red fur with long sharp claws; his mark was an axe-like hump growing from his chest, used to cleave enemies in two.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita, Ochokochi digambarkan sebagai monster raksasa berbulu merah karat dengan cakar panjang tajam; cirinya tonjolan seperti kapak yang tumbuh dari dada, dipakai untuk membelah lawan menjadi dua.
claims.quote: Согласно преданиям, Очокочи представлялся огромным, покрытым рыжей (цвета ржавчины) шерстью чудовищем с длинными острыми когтями. Отличительной особенностью Очокочи был топорообразный горб, росший из грудной клетки, используемый им, чтобы рассекать противников надвое.

claims.statement: He is infatuated with the beauty of the Queen of the Forest, Tkashi-Mapa, and chases her, but hunters visiting her forest often thwart him.
claims.statement_id: Ia tergila-gila pada kecantikan Ratu Hutan, Tkashi-Mapa, dan terus mengejarnya, tetapi usahanya sering digagalkan para pemburu yang mendatangi hutannya.
claims.quote: He is infatuated by the beauty of the Queen of the Forest, Tkashi-Mapa, after whom he chases. However, his attempts to catch her are often thwarted by the hunters who visit her forest.

claims.statement: An Ochokochi killed by hunters could also revive after a second shot or sword blow.
claims.statement_id: Ochokochi yang dibunuh pemburu juga dapat hidup kembali setelah tembakan atau tebasan pedang kedua.
claims.quote: Убитый охотниками Очокочи имел также способность оживать после повторного выстрела или удара меча.

claims.statement: Ochokochi is the most common figure of children's scary tales, still used in western Georgia to frighten naughty children.
claims.statement_id: Ochokochi adalah tokoh paling umum dalam cerita seram anak-anak, yang sampai kini dipakai untuk menakuti anak-anak nakal di Georgia Barat.
claims.quote: Очокочи является наиболее распространённым персонажем детских страшилок, которыми до сих пор в Западной Грузии пугают непослушных детей .

claims.statement: In Mingrelian mythology Ochokochi is a deity protecting game animals, the antagonist of Tkashi-Mapa.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Mingrelia, Ochokochi adalah dewa pelindung binatang buruan, antagonis Tkashi-Mapa (ტყაშმაფა).
claims.quote: ოჩოკოჩი — მეგრულ მითოლოგიაში ნადირთმფარველი ღვთაება, ტყაშმაფას ანტაგონისტი.

claims.statement: Ochokochi could not speak, but his rumbling voice filled people with indescribable fear; the closest figure to him is Pan of ancient Greek myth, likewise half-man, half-goat.
claims.statement_id: Ochokochi tidak dapat berbicara, tetapi suaranya yang bergemuruh membuat orang sangat ketakutan; tokoh yang paling dekat dengannya adalah Pan (Пан) dari mitos Yunani kuno, yang juga setengah manusia setengah kambing.
claims.quote: Очокочи был лишён дара речи, но звуки его рокочущего голоса повергали людей в неописуемый страх. Очокочи наиболее близок персонаж древнегреческих мифов Пан, являвшийся подобно Очокочи получеловеком-полукозлом

claims.statement: Pereplut is a Slavic deity or demon of unclear function, appearing in the list of gods and demons of the 12th-century Ruthenian interpolation of the Word of St. Grigory (manuscript from the 15th century) and in the Word of St. John.
claims.statement_id: Pereplut adalah dewa atau iblis Slavia yang fungsinya tidak jelas; ia muncul dalam daftar dewa dan iblis pada sisipan Rutenia abad ke-12 dalam Kata Santo Grigory (Word of St. Grigory, naskahnya dari abad ke-15), juga dalam Kata Santo Yohanes (Word of St. John).
claims.quote: Pereplut is a Slavic deity or a demon with an unclear function. It appears in the list of gods and demons of the 12th-century Ruthenian interpolation of the Word of St. Grigory (the manuscript itself dates from the 15th century), as well as in the Word of St. John.

claims.statement: Pereplut's name may have been distorted in copying; the spinning and drinking mentioned are probably traces of magic rites with dance and libation.
claims.statement_id: Nama Pereplut mungkin terdistorsi saat penyalinan naskah; putaran dan minum yang disebut mungkin jejak ritus magis dengan unsur tarian dan persembahan minuman.
claims.quote: Pereplut's name may have been distorted when copying the manuscript. The mentioned spinning and drinking are probably traces of magical rituals with elements of dance and libation.

claims.statement: Alexei Sobolewski considered Pereplut a demon ensuring prosperity when crossing river rapids, hence possibly a water deity, from pere- "through" and pluti- "to flow".
claims.statement_id: Alexei Sobolewski menganggap Pereplut iblis yang menjamin keselamatan saat melewati jeram sungai, sehingga mungkin dewa air, dengan etimologi pere- "melalui" dan pluti- "mengalir".
claims.quote: considering Pereplut to be a demon ensuring prosperity when crossing river thresholds, hence his possible identification as a water deity, with the etymology of the words pere- "through" and pluti-"to flow".

claims.statement: Stanisław Urbańczyk reconstructed the theonym as Pereput, and Boris Rybakov considered it a new name variant of the archaic deity Simargl.
claims.statement_id: Stanisław Urbańczyk merekonstruksi nama dewa ini sebagai Pereput, dan Boris Rybakov menganggapnya variasi nama baru dari dewa kuno Simargl.
claims.quote: This etymology was adopted by Stanisław Urbańczyk, who reconstructed the theonym in the form of Pereput. Boris Rybakov considered it a new name variation of archaic deity Simargl.

claims.statement: Pereplut is mentioned among other pagan gods in the Word of St. Gregory (Sofia copy), which says only that people drank in his honour "turning in the horns".
claims.statement_id: Pereplut (Переплут) disebut di antara dewa pagan lain dalam Kata Santo Grigory (Слово святого Григория) menurut salinan Sofia, yang hanya menyebut bahwa orang minum untuk menghormati Pereplut sambil berputar ("вертячеся в розех"); karena tak ada data lain, tak ada yang pasti tentangnya.
claims.quote: Переплут среди других языческих богов упоминается в «Слове святого Григория», цитируемом по софийскому списку, где сообщается лишь, что в честь Переплута пили, «вертячеся в розех».

claims.statement: Aleksander Brückner considered Pereplut a demon of fate.
claims.statement_id: Aleksander Brückner menganggap Pereplut (Perepłut) iblis takdir.
claims.quote: Aleksander Brückner z kolei uważał Perepłuta za demona losu

claims.statement: Max Vasmer called him "patron god of seafarers" and derived the name from pere- and Proto-Slavic *plovǫ, *pluti, "to sail".
claims.statement_id: Max Vasmer (М. Фасмер) menyebutnya "dewa pelindung pelaut" dan menurunkan namanya dari пере- dan Proto-Slavia *plovǫ, *pluti, "berlayar".
claims.quote: М. Фасмер называет его «богом-покровитель мореходов» и выводит этимологию от пере- и праслав. *plovǫ, *pluti «плыть».
